plan_content.architectural_approach: Independence lens: I read from the consumer and contract end backward — enforcement step, then observe payload outputs, then the header's stated invariant, then the job gate — and met the changed code last, so the plan is anchored on the file's own declared contract rather than on implementation shape. The architectural move is to make the code honor the invariant it already states: dispatch the healthcheck outcome through an explicit exit-class case (docker-refusal 125/126/127 versus the probe's own exit status) so the branch that prints rpo=breached is unreachable when the probe could not run, mirroring the case dispatch the dr_observed branch already uses. Fail-closed is preserved, not weakened: indeterminate still fails the run, but with a message that names the cannot-tell class instead of asserting a breach. One bounded retry on the cannot-tell class only (single re-exec within the existing 120-second SSH command budget) hardens against the mid-restart transient the header itself names, without ever retrying a verdict. Boundary honesty: the healthcheck script's internal exit semantics are external to this file and are honored as verdicts when the script actually ran; what becomes structurally impossible is emitting a breach verdict the probe never produced.
plan_content.context: What this workflow is and why the failure matters, in cause/effect terms. A junior engineer should read it this way: (1) every five minutes, GitHub schedules this workflow on main; its only product is a green or red check plus step logs — if it fails persistently, operators either page on it or learn to ignore it, and an ignored RPO monitor is functionally absent. (2) The probe step SSHes to the production droplet and runs a payload that reports what production PROVES: dr_observed=present|absent|indeterminate, and, when archiving is present, rpo=healthy|breached. (3) The file's header states the governing invariant: only the first two observations are verdicts; 'could not tell' fails closed in resolve-dr-activation.sh rather than guessing — this discipline exists because the previous single docker exec collapsed everything into an opaque exit 127 (the INFRA-CRITICAL-195 history referenced in recent commits). (4) The rpo branch breaks that invariant: 'if docker exec ... postgres-walg-healthcheck.sh; then healthy else breached' treats docker-level refusal (daemon error 125, not-executable 126, not-found 127 — the probe never ran) identically to the healthcheck running and reporting the RPO budget unmet. Effect: a container mid-restart or an image whose script path moved produces a standing 'PRODUCTION WAL ARCHIVE RPO BREACH' alarm on main every five minutes, indistinguishable in the check status from a real breach. (5) If skipped, the next real breach is masked by noise and the invariant spec that runs this payload keeps locking the conflation in. Evidence proving the result after the fix: the failing run's step name plus the new class-labeled error message name exactly which of the three states fired, and the declared test command keeps the spec that executes this payload green.

key_changes.description: Diagnose the root cause of the failing 'Database WAL Archive Freshness' run on head 08b0f4d19fce2484ad528d45b0ebd903e7c1e71f and land the architectural fix, touching only .github/workflows/database-wal-archive-freshness.yml. Step A (diagnosis): read the failing run's log and record which of the five failure exits fired — 'Require protected main authority' (ref mismatch), 'Assert protected backup environment is complete' (missing DROPLET_* secrets), 'Observe production WAL archive runtime' (SSH transport or unrecognizable observation), 'Resolve declared activation against production' (declared/observed drift in either direction, or indeterminate failing closed), or 'Enforce the five-minute RPO' (rpo != healthy while active). Step B (fix, same file): in the observe payload's rpo branch, capture the docker exec exit status and classify it — exit 125/126/127 means the probe could not run: retry once after a short sleep within the existing 120-second command budget, and if it still cannot run print 'rpo=indeterminate'; a probe that ran and returned non-zero prints 'rpo=breached'; zero prints 'rpo=healthy'. In the observe step's output guard, additionally validate that rpo is one of healthy|breached|indeterminate whenever observed=present, so an empty or garbled rpo cannot flow onward. In the 'Enforce the five-minute RPO' step, distinguish three outcomes: healthy passes with the existing success message; breached keeps the existing breach error; indeterminate fails closed with an error that names the cannot-tell class and the retry result instead of asserting a breach. Leave the DR_CAPABILITY/DR_OBSERVED interface to resolve-dr-activation.sh, the env-scrubbed run-protected-ssh.sh invocation, and the payload's stdout key=value contract unchanged.

plan_steps_detailed: 1. Diagnosis (no file edit): open the failing run at head 08b0f4d and identify the failed step. Each of the five steps is one root-cause class; record the class and the step's error line in the commit message. This is mechanical because each class has a distinct step name.

2. Observe payload rpo branch: replace the unconditional if/else around 'docker exec aqua-postgres /usr/local/bin/postgres-walg-healthcheck.sh' with exit-class dispatch: capture the exec status; 125/126/127 -> single bounded retry (short sleep, one re-exec, still inside SSH_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=120), still cannot-run -> printf 'rpo=indeterminate'; ran and non-zero -> 'rpo=breached'; zero -> 'rpo=healthy'. Never retry a verdict.

3. Observe step output guard: extend the existing case validation so that when observed=present, rpo must match healthy|breached|indeterminate; anything else hits the existing 'no recognisable observation' error path.

4. Enforcement step: three labeled outcomes — healthy: existing success message; breached: existing 'PRODUCTION WAL ARCHIVE RPO BREACH' error; indeterminate: fail closed with an error naming the cannot-tell class and the retry result, citing that a verdict was not obtainable.

5. Interface freeze: DR_OBSERVED/DR_CAPABILITY inputs to resolve-dr-activation.sh, the assert-backup-secrets.sh invocation, the run-protected-ssh.sh env-scrubbed invocation, and the payload stdout key=value shape all remain byte-compatible except for the one new rpo value.
6. Commit with the diagnosed root-cause class named, then run both declared validation commands.

plan_content.architectural_approach: Tier 2 (make the correct behaviour the zero-effort default), achieved per defect: (1) the CORS matcher makes loopback-only approval the default response of the dev server — no per-developer action, no per-line pragma, and any non-loopback origin is refused structurally by configuration; (2) the spread-first key order makes the documented project-level test contract win by construction — precedence is enforced by object-literal evaluation order itself, so the project setup file cannot be shadowed without an explicit, visible edit to these lines. Both fixes are declarative and local; neither adds imports (imports: []) nor touches any file outside web/modules/admin-panel/vite.config.ts.
plan_content.context: Task, taught plainly: F-014 cites two lines of the admin-panel microfrontend's Vite config, and the fix must land in that one file. Start from the consumers and work backward. Consumer 1 is the module-federation host: in dev it fetches http://localhost:3004/remotes/admin-panel/remoteEntry.js cross-origin, which is why the server block has CORS at all — but 'cors: true' (line 47) answers 'yes' to EVERY Origin header, so any web page you have open can read responses from your dev server, not just the shell. Consumer 2 is the test runner: the 'test' object feeds all 50 spec files of project web-admin-panel, and its last key is the spread of the shared policy factory '...createVitestTestPolicy()' (line 57). In JavaScript object literals a later spread wins, so the shared policy silently outranks 'environment', 'globals', and 'setupFiles' (lines 54-56) — yet the comment at lines 51-52 calls exactly those keys 'a project-level runtime contract'. If libs/testing ever defines 'setupFiles', this project's setup file stops loading with no error and no failing test: that is the failure this plan removes. If skipped, the over-open CORS posture persists and the next change to the shared policy can silently alter test runtime for this module. Downstream surfaces: the shell's dev-time fetch of remoteEntry.js, the nx 'test' target of web-admin-panel with its 50 spec files, and the read-only contracts this config consumes (libs/testing policy factory, web/shared-ui federation helpers, pagination/shared-contracts aliases) — none of which are written. Evidence: the cited lines themselves in the provided excerpt; the three overlapping excerpts agree byte-for-byte on their overlap, which is the fidelity check used here because no file tools were available in this run to recompute the excerpt hashes.

key_changes.description: Edit web/modules/admin-panel/vite.config.ts only. (1) Line 47: keep 'port: 3004' and 'strictPort: true' unchanged and replace 'cors: true' with a restricted origin policy: cors: { origin: /^https?:\/\/(localhost|127\.0\.0\.1|\[::1\])(:\d+)?$/ } — the config declares no server.host, so Vite binds loopback by default and every origin that can legitimately reach this remote is a loopback origin on an arbitrary port (the shell dev server). (2) Lines 53-57: move the '...createVitestTestPolicy()' spread to the FIRST key of the 'test' object so the keys that follow — 'environment: jsdom', 'globals: true', 'setupFiles: ["./src/test-setup.ts"]' (line 56) — take precedence over any same-named key the shared policy defines; the three values and the policy spread itself stay byte-identical, only key order changes. Keep formatting compliant with the repository format gate.

plan_steps_detailed: 1. Confirm the working tree matches the excerpt: server block at line 47 reads 'server: { port: 3004, strictPort: true, cors: true }' and the test block at lines 53-57 lists environment/globals/setupFiles before the createVitestTestPolicy() spread. If the file drifted, stop and surface the mismatch instead of editing blind.

2. Line 47 edit: replace 'cors: true' with 'cors: { origin: /^https?:\/\/(localhost|127\.0\.0\.1|\[::1\])(:\d+)?$/ }', keeping 'port: 3004' and 'strictPort: true' exactly as they are. Rationale chain: no server.host in this config -> Vite binds loopback -> every origin able to reach the dev server is loopback -> reflecting arbitrary origins grants nothing legitimate and exposes dev responses to any page.

3. Test-block edit: move '...createVitestTestPolicy()' to be the first key inside 'test', followed by 'environment: "jsdom"', 'globals: true', 'setupFiles: ["./src/test-setup.ts"]'. Change nothing else in the object; the policy's non-colliding keys (include, coverage, mock settings, etc.) continue to apply unchanged.
4. Run the four declared validation commands and require exit 0 on each; 'npx nx affected --target=test' is the decisive gate because it executes the 50 spec files under the reordered test object.
5. If any validation fails, revert the file (see rollback) and report rather than iterating outside the allowed surface.
plan_content.recursive_impact: Closure is the single nx project web-admin-panel (layer 3), which the changed path itself reaches. Inside it: (a) the project's test target and its 50 spec files inherit the reordered test object — the reorder only changes which side wins on key collision, and is verified by 'npx nx affected --target=test'; (b) dev-time consumers of remoteEntry.js see a CORS response restricted to loopback origins — production serving is unaffected because it does not use this dev-server option; (c) build/preview outputs are untouched (no change to exposes, shared, base, build.target). No event-contract, NATS consumer, entity, or migration surface is touched, so the machine closure adds no nodes beyond project:web-admin-panel; no waivers are needed. The read-only contracts (libs/testing/vitest policy, web/shared-ui federation config and alias helper, platform/libs/pagination-contracts, libs/shared-contracts) are consumed, never written; notably the reorder fix is correct regardless of what keys the policy factory returns, so the plan does not depend on unread internals of libs/testing.

plan_content.summary: Independent consumer-first scan of web/modules/admin-panel/vite.config.ts finds exactly two remediable defects on the cited lines. plan_content.title: Fix failing CI workflow 'Deploy Capacity Maintenance' (run #38409794036)

plan_content.architectural_approach: Defect chain, stated as cause and effect: the script does 'cd /var/aqua-saas' — the file's own comment documents this is a bare object store, not a working tree — then 'git fetch --force --prune origin main'. A shorthand refspec fetch writes FETCH_HEAD only; a bare clone has no configured remote.origin.fetch refspec, so no opportunistic remote-tracking update creates or refreshes refs/remotes/origin/main. The next line, 'TARGET_SHA="$(git rev-parse origin/main)"', resolves the 'origin/main' shorthand against exactly those remote-tracking refs — which the store does not guarantee to exist. Under 'set -euo pipefail' that resolution failure exits the step before checkout bootstrap, failing every scheduled and dispatched run identically. Even if the store happens to carry local configuration that makes the shorthand resolve today, depending on undocumented store state is itself the defect. Fix, tier 2 (make the correct behaviour the zero-effort default): fetch with the fully-qualified refspec '+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main' and read 'refs/remotes/origin/main' — the write and the read name the identical fully-qualified ref in adjacent commands, so correct pinning requires no operator effort and no store-side setup, and the failure mode has no ambient state left to depend on.
plan_content.context: What this lane is and why the failure matters: 'Deploy Capacity Maintenance' is the production droplet's 6-hourly capacity lane. Each production deploy pulls a fresh image per service (~1.85GB x 13) and leaves the prior generation untagged; this workflow's safe-image-gc keeps the droplet under the capacity-preflight threshold so deploys do not block — the workflow's own header names run #695 / 28332208818 / 28330781676 as the historic blocked-deploy outcome. The job (line 54) has one SSH step (line 59) that must: derive and validate a GHCR image prefix from github.repository (INFRA-CRITICAL-085: no dispatch input names a release, image, registry or repository), resolve the remote's current main to a pinned SHA on the droplet's bare object store, bootstrap the immutable deploy checkout from that SHA, and run scripts/deploy/droplet-capacity.sh from it. It is failing on head 99689e46bd86eb980ca2bad74df3c6b072eb4e90. The task: diagnose the root cause and land the architectural fix touching only this workflow file. If it is skipped or mis-fixed, untagged generations accumulate until production deploys are capacity-blocked — the exact outage class this lane exists to prevent; the downstream surface is the deploy control plane's capacity preflight and the droplet's disk headroom.

key_changes.description: Root-cause fix in the capacity-maintenance step's script block (the step whose name begins 'Run capacity operation through production deploy control plane'). Replace the two lines 'git fetch --force --prune origin main' and 'TARGET_SHA="$(git rev-parse origin/main)"' with 'git fetch --force --prune origin +refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main' and 'TARGET_SHA="$(git rev-parse refs/remotes/origin/main)"'. Effect: the fetch explicitly writes the fully-qualified remote-tracking ref and the pin reads that same fully-qualified ref, so SHA resolution cannot depend on the bare store's ambient refspec configuration; 'cd /var/aqua-saas', the DEPLOY_SHA export, and everything after (install -d /var/lib/aqua/deploy, git show of deploy-paths.sh, materialize_deploy_checkout, the OPERATION case block) stay byte-identical.

Adjacent hardening in the same script block, same file: immediately after 'export DEPLOY_SHA="${TARGET_SHA}"' add 'printf "capacity lane pinned to %s\n" "${DEPLOY_SHA}"' so the resolved pin is visible in the job log for triage, and add a short comment above the fetch stating the invariant — the store is bare and carries no remote-tracking configuration guarantee, so the lane must fetch and read the same fully-qualified ref — so a future editor cannot silently regress to shorthand resolution.

plan_content.summary: The capacity-maintenance job fails in its single SSH step when it pins the target SHA: the script fetches 'main' into the droplet's bare object store with a shorthand refspec (which writes FETCH_HEAD only, since bare stores carry no remote.origin.fetch refspec to update opportunistically) and then resolves the 'origin/main' shorthand, which depends on remote-tracking refs the store does not maintain; under 'set -euo pipefail' the step exits before checkout bootstrap and the 6-hourly GC lane fails on every scheduled and manual run. The fix, entirely inside the one allowed file, makes SHA resolution configuration-independent: fetch with the fully-qualified refspec '+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main' and read 'refs/remotes/origin/main', so the ref written and the ref read are the same name in adjacent commands. This is tier 2 — correct resolution becomes the zero-effort default with no reliance on undocumented store state. Residual risk: run logs are not admissible evidence here, so if the observed failure sits past bootstrap (inside scripts/deploy/droplet-capacity.sh at the target commit, or at the SSH command_timeout) the fix locus is outside allowed_scope and the round must widen scope instead of landing this edit.

plan_content.architectural_approach: Tier 2 — make the correct behaviour automatic. Today the correct CI status for a completed maintenance sweep requires a human to look at a red check and mentally reclassify it as 'expected while degraded'; after the change, green-when-the-bounded-contract-completed is the zero-effort default, and degradation becomes a surfaced, greppable warning instead of a false maintenance failure. Blocking semantics are preserved where they belong: manual 'gate' dispatch propagates the raw verdict, and the deploy-time gate in the deploy workflows is independent of this lane. A Tier-3 detectability component rides along: stage markers plus RC capture make any future failure self-locating, which also closes the diagnosis loop that the evidence set (file only, no logs) could not. The capacity finding itself is never hidden — it is reclassified to a non-blocking, explicitly-marked channel while every hard-failure class (bootstrap errors, script kills, timeouts, unsupported operation) stays red.
plan_content.context: What this lane does, for orientation: every 6 hours (cron, line 15) GitHub Actions SSHes to the production droplet, resolves origin/main inside the bare store /var/aqua-saas, bootstraps the canonical immutable deploy checkout from that exact SHA, and runs scripts/deploy/droplet-capacity.sh — 'report' or 'gate' for manual dispatch, 'gate' with CAPACITY_GC_MODE=auto for the scheduled sweep that reclaims superseded images (~1.85GB x 13 per deploy generation per the header). Why the failure shape matters: the CI run on head 99689e46 failed with annotations anchored at the job (line 54) and the single step (line 59), i.e. the SSH step exited non-zero — but the evidence set contains no run log, so the diagnosis must come from the file's structure. The structural cause: under 'set -euo pipefail' the script's last command is the capacity gate (line 110), and the header itself (lines 5-14) defines that gate as a deploy-blocking control that 'blocks' when disk accumulates. A maintenance lane whose success criterion is a deploy-blocking gate will report itself as failed precisely in the situation it exists to manage — whenever the bounded GC cannot fully clear the capacity class (non-image disk growth such as volumes, logs, or build cache under the pull-only ADR-033 runtime, or a residual class after the sweep stops at its bound). What breaks if this is skipped: a permanently or frequently red scheduled check that trains operators to ignore it, hiding genuine regressions in the bootstrap chain inside the noise. Downstream surfaces affected by the fix: the scheduled lane's own CI status (intended), any branch-protection rule that references this workflow by name (its meaning changes from 'capacity healthy' to 'maintenance executed' — documented in kc-3), and nothing on the droplet itself, since the same script, environment, and bounds are run unchanged.

key_changes.description: Instrument the SSH script in .github/workflows/deploy-capacity-maintenance.yml with greppable stage markers and explicit exit-code capture. Echo a line like '[capacity-maintenance] stage=image-prefix' around the IMAGE_PREFIX derivation/validation, 'stage=bare-store-fetch' around the /var/aqua-saas fetch and rev-parse, 'stage=checkout-bootstrap' around the deploy-paths.sh bootstrap and materialize_deploy_checkout, and 'stage=capacity-op' around the droplet-capacity.sh invocation. Replace the unconditional capacity invocation in the case branch with 'set +e; CAPACITY_GC_MODE=auto CAPACITY_DISK_USAGE_MODE=deep bash scripts/deploy/droplet-capacity.sh gate; RC=$?; set -e' so the gate's verdict is captured rather than terminating the script. This makes each future failure localize to its exact stage in the run log (the current evidence anchors only the job at line 54 and the step at line 59) and is the in-band instrument that confirms or refutes the structural diagnosis on the next run.

Split the shared 'safe-image-gc | gate' case branch (line 109) into two branches with distinct success contracts. safe-image-gc (the scheduled maintenance path, OPERATION fallback at line 65): if RC=0 exit 0 unchanged; if RC!=0 emit a distinct non-blocking marker — echo '::warning::capacity maintenance completed its bounded sweep; capacity class not cleared — full gate output above' and 'MAINTENANCE-OUTCOME=capacity-degraded' — then exit 0. gate (manual workflow_dispatch): propagate RC unchanged so a human-dispatched capacity check remains blocking. Everything before the case statement (bootstrap chain, lines 88-103) stays under 'set -e' and remains a hard failure, and kills at command_timeout 12m (line 76) or timeout-minutes 15 (line 56) never reach the classifier, so only returned gate verdicts are reclassified. Net effect: the lane's CI status asserts 'the bounded maintenance executed' automatically, while the deploy lane's own capacity preflight remains the blocking capacity control.

Update the header comment block (lines 5-14) and the OPERATION-fallback comment (lines 62-64) to state the lane's success contract explicitly: scheduled safe-image-gc equals bounded sweep executed (green); residual capacity class equals warning marker in the log with the blocking control living in the deploy-time gate; infrastructure/bootstrap errors and timeout kills equal red. Note in the comment that the remote '::warning::' and '::error::' strings are log markers, not GitHub annotations, because appleboy/ssh-action does not forward workflow commands emitted on the droplet — which is also true of the existing '::error::' uses in the script today.

plan_steps_detailed: 1. kc-1: add stage markers and convert the capacity invocation in the case branch to captured-RC form (set +e ... RC=$? ... set -e).
2. kc-2: split 'safe-image-gc | gate' into two branches; scheduled GC path exits 0 with a warning marker on RC!=0; manual gate path propagates RC.
3. kc-3: update header and OPERATION-fallback comments to document the success contract and the marker-not-annotation nature of remote workflow-command strings.

4. Verify: run the declared validation commands; after landing, inspect the next scheduled run's log for the stage markers and outcome marker, and confirm a manual operation=gate dispatch on a degraded droplet still exits non-zero.

plan_content.summary: Failing CI workflow 'Deploy Capacity Maintenance' (.github/workflows/deploy-capacity-maintenance.yml) on head 99689e46bd86eb980ca2bad74df3c6b072eb4e90; diagnose root cause + land architectural fix.
plan_content.title: Fix failing CI workflow 'Deploy Capacity Maintenance' (run #38409794036)

plan_content.architectural_approach: Ranking every stage of the failing step by how it can fail: the env plumbing cannot fail on valid input; the IMAGE_PREFIX derivation fails only through its own explicit regex ::error with a named cause; the downstream capacity scripts are invoked from a pinned immutable checkout. The one stage that is both unguarded and rests on a fresh layout assumption is the host-side SHA resolution: reading 'origin/main' presumes the bare store maintains refs/remotes/origin/*, but a bare clone or mirror keeps heads under refs/heads/*, and 'git fetch origin main' with no matching configured refspec writes only FETCH_HEAD — under 'set -euo pipefail' the subsequent 'git rev-parse origin/main' then aborts the whole step with a bare git error and no stage attribution. That is also the newest code path at this head, which fits a failure that begins at this head. The architectural fix is to make the fetch write exactly the ref the script reads (+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main) and to peel-verify that ref to a commit, so the fetch/read pair cannot silently diverge on any store layout — the correct resolution becomes the zero-effort default (tier 2), and any residual store corruption surfaces as a named ::error instead of an anonymous abort. The FETCH_HEAD-only alternative was considered and rejected: FETCH_HEAD is shared mutable state that the deploy lane also writes, so a dedicated ref is the deterministic contract. The same change adds a git cat-file -e existence check for the deploy-paths helper so the last unguarded assumption in the chain is also stage-named.
plan_content.context: What this workflow does and why it matters, for someone seeing it cold: 'Deploy Capacity Maintenance' is the production droplet's capacity lane. Every 6 hours by schedule (or on manual dispatch) the job at line 54 runs one SSH step (line 59) that resolves the remote's current main on the host, bootstraps the canonical deploy checkout from that exact commit, and runs scripts/deploy/droplet-capacity.sh in report or gate mode (the scheduled default is the safe image GC gate). The file's own schedule comment explains the stakes: each production deploy pulls a fresh ~1.85GB image per service across 13 services, leaving the prior generation untagged; without this bounded sweep those generations accumulate until the deploy capacity-preflight gate blocks deploys. So the downstream surface of this lane failing is not just a red CI badge — it is every subsequent production deploy's capacity preflight, which starts failing again once disk pressure rebuilds. The reported failure is on head 99689e46bd86eb980ca2bad74df3c6b072eb4e90, and the only admissible evidence is the workflow file itself, so the diagnosis must come from reading the step's own dependency chain.

key_changes.description: In the capacity-maintenance SSH script, replace the implicit origin/main resolution with an explicit ref contract and stage-named failures: (1) 'if ! git fetch --force --prune origin "+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main"; then echo "::error::capacity-maintenance: git fetch of origin/main failed in /var/aqua-saas"; exit 2; fi' so the fetch writes exactly the ref that is read, on any bare-store layout; (2) 'if ! TARGET_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify "refs/remotes/origin/main^{commit}")"; then echo "::error::capacity-maintenance: refs/remotes/origin/main did not resolve to a commit after fetch"; exit 2; fi' then 'export DEPLOY_SHA="${TARGET_SHA}"'; (3) before the existing 'git show', add 'if ! git cat-file -e "${TARGET_SHA}:scripts/deploy/deploy-paths.sh" 2>/dev/null; then echo "::error::capacity-maintenance: scripts/deploy/deploy-paths.sh absent at ${TARGET_SHA}"; exit 2; fi'. Leave the IMAGE_PREFIX derivation and regex guard, the install -d bootstrap, source of deploy-paths.sh, materialize_deploy_checkout, cd into DEPLOY_CHECKOUT_DIR, and the OPERATION case dispatch byte-identical.

plan_steps_detailed.action: Edit the SSH script in .github/workflows/deploy-capacity-maintenance.yml: after 'cd /var/aqua-saas', replace 'git fetch --force --prune origin main' with a guarded explicit-refspec fetch writing refs/remotes/origin/main, and replace 'TARGET_SHA="$(git rev-parse origin/main)"' with a guarded 'git rev-parse --verify refs/remotes/origin/main^{commit}'. Exact replacement fragment: 'if ! git fetch --force --prune origin "+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main"; then echo "::error::capacity-maintenance: git fetch of origin/main failed in /var/aqua-saas"; exit 2; fi' and 'if ! TARGET_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify "refs/remotes/origin/main^{commit}")"; then echo "::error::capacity-maintenance: refs/remotes/origin/main did not resolve to a commit after fetch"; exit 2; fi', keeping 'export DEPLOY_SHA="${TARGET_SHA}"'.
plan_steps_detailed.why: Cause/effect: the fetch now writes the exact ref the read consumes, so no ambient repository configuration can make the read fail after a successful fetch; if the fetch itself fails, the log names the stage instead of aborting anonymously.

plan_steps_detailed.action: Immediately before the existing 'git show "${TARGET_SHA}:scripts/deploy/deploy-paths.sh" > /var/lib/aqua/deploy/deploy-paths.sh' line, add: 'if ! git cat-file -e "${TARGET_SHA}:scripts/deploy/deploy-paths.sh" 2>/dev/null; then echo "::error::capacity-maintenance: scripts/deploy/deploy-paths.sh absent at ${TARGET_SHA}"; exit 2; fi'. Change nothing else in the script: IMAGE_PREFIX derivation and regex guard, install -d, source of deploy-paths.sh, materialize_deploy_checkout, cd into DEPLOY_CHECKOUT_DIR, and the OPERATION case dispatch stay byte-identical.
plan_steps_detailed.why: This converts the last unguarded host-side assumption (helper path exists at the resolved SHA) into a named, diagnosable failure, so whatever stage actually fails on the next run, the log identifies it by name.

plan_steps_detailed.action: Run the declared validation commands; confirm the format gate accepts the edited YAML. The runtime proof is the next lane execution: an operator-dispatched run with operation=report either passes end to end or emits exactly one stage-named ::error identifying the true failing stage — either outcome is evidence that closes the diagnosis loop.
plan_steps_detailed.why: None of the executable gates runs the workflow itself, so the plan's verification story is explicit: static gates now, and the instrumented next run as the runtime witness.

plan_content.recursive_impact: Traversal order (consumer end first, changed code last): (1) Consumers of this lane's effect — the deploy capacity-preflight gate that depends on the droplet staying under threshold, and operators reading run logs when it does not. If the lane fails silently or anonymously, disk pressure returns and deploys block, the exact failure class the schedule comment documents. (2) The step's dependency chain, backward from execution order: scripts/deploy/droplet-capacity.sh subcommands (report/gate with CAPACITY_GC_MODE, CAPACITY_DISK_USAGE_MODE, DEPLOY_SERVICES, FULL_DEPLOY) depend on the materialized checkout; the checkout depends on materialize_deploy_checkout and DEPLOY_CHECKOUT_DIR from scripts/deploy/deploy-paths.sh at the resolved SHA; that bootstrap depends on 'git show <SHA>:scripts/deploy/deploy-paths.sh'; the SHA depends on 'git rev-parse origin/main' after 'git fetch --force --prune origin main' inside /var/aqua-saas — which the file's own comment block describes as the persistent bare object store, not an executable working tree; and the env plumbing (OPERATION, FULL_DEPLOY, DEPLOY_SERVICES, IMAGE_REPOSITORY from github.repository) feeds all of it. (3) Machine impact closure of the touched path: a GitHub workflow YAML maps to no Nx project, no event-contract subscriber, and no entity/migration node — the closure is the file itself, so no coverage waivers are required.

risks.mitigation: The same change instruments every resolution stage with a stage-named ::error, so the next run's log names the true failing stage; the fix is therefore evidence-generating even where the primary hypothesis is wrong.
risks.summary: Root-cause diagnosis is derived from the workflow file alone; no run log was admissible evidence, so if the actual failure is elsewhere — for example missing DROPLET_* secrets in the production environment, deployment protection rules holding scheduled runs, or the 12m command_timeout exceeded by deep disk-usage scans — the refspec fix alone will not clear the red run.

risks.mitigation: This lane only fetches and never mirror-pushes, the ref write is namespaced under refs/remotes/, and the file's concurrency group serializes this workflow's own runs; no consumer of refs/heads/* is affected.
risks.summary: Writing refs/remotes/origin/main into a mirror-layout bare store is an additive ref write that other readers of /var/aqua-saas did not previously observe.

risks.mitigation: Stated plainly in the validation plan rather than left implicit: static gates land with the change, and the instrumented next run is the runtime witness; the added ::error lines exist precisely to make that witness legible.
risks.summary: None of the declared validation commands executes the workflow, so YAML runtime validity is proven only by the next scheduled or dispatched run.

plan_content.rollback: The change is a single-file edit with no infrastructure state mutation of its own — it only changes how refs are resolved before the existing bounded operations run. Rollback is 'git revert' of the one commit touching .github/workflows/deploy-capacity-maintenance.yml, restoring the exact prior script. Roll back only on evidence the new refspec fetch broke a previously-green path (e.g., a store hook rejecting ref writes); note that reverting also restores the currently-failing resolution behavior, so the revert decision needs the failing run's log, not just a red check.
plan_content.summary: The capacity-maintenance job fails at head 99689e46bd86eb980ca2bad74df3c6b072eb4e90 inside the single SSH step that runs the droplet-side control plane. Traversing the step's dependency chain backward from its consumers, every stage either cannot fail on valid input (env plumbing), fails with its own named ::error (the IMAGE_PREFIX regex guard), or runs guarded downstream scripts — except the newest, unguarded stage: 'git fetch --force --prune origin main' followed by 'git rev-parse origin/main' inside /var/aqua-saas, a repository the file itself documents as a bare object store where remote-tracking refs are not guaranteed to exist. The fix pins the fetch to write exactly the ref the script reads (+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main), verifies it peels to a commit, and gives every remaining resolution stage a stage-named ::error so the next run log identifies the failing stage by name regardless of which assumption was wrong. The change touches only .github/workflows/deploy-capacity-maintenance.yml.
plan_content.title: Deploy Capacity Maintenance: make the host-side main-resolution an explicit fetch-to-read ref contract with stage-named failures
plan_content.validation_plan: Declared executable gates (all four from the canonical suite): npx nx affected --target=test; npx nx affected --target=lint; npm run type-check; node tools/quality/quality.mjs format check-changed — the format gate is the one that parses the changed YAML. These prove the edit is statically sound. The runtime proof, which no sandboxed command can provide, is the next execution of the lane: the scheduled run or a manual workflow_dispatch with operation=report (12m command budget, 15m job budget). Success criteria: exit 0 with the capacity report emitted; or a single stage-named ::error line (fetch / sha-resolve / helper-missing) that converts the following round's diagnosis from inference to observation.

risks.summary: Primary revision plan-cyc-20261013T160841Z-auto-r1 carries no plan_content.architectural_tier; the kernel refuses the body at submit and at the plan_contract_complete gate (plan_architectural_tier_missing), so the round cannot converge on it as delivered.

risks.recommendation: Adopt the challenger's evidence-anchored diagnosis (in the bare store /var/aqua-saas the fetch 'git fetch --force --prune origin main' writes FETCH_HEAD only when no remote refspec is configured, so 'git rev-parse origin/main' aborts under set -euo pipefail) or supply an independent one, and prescribe the exact guarded edit fragment for the SSH script.
risks.summary: Primary's sole key change (ci-run-38409794036-key-change-001) restates the task — 'diagnose root cause + land architectural fix' — with no root-cause hypothesis and no edit content; an implementer applying it exactly as the key-change-0 obligation prescribes would receive no change prescription at all, leaving the failing step at line 59 unfixed.

risks.recommendation: Whichever body converges must keep the stage-named error instrumentation (fetch / sha-resolve / helper-missing) so the next lane run converts inference to observation; treat a still-red instrumented run as new evidence for the following round, not as a silent verdict on the refspec change.
risks.summary: No run log was admissible, so the refspec root cause is inference from the workflow file alone; alternate causes visible in the same job — production-environment protection rules on the job at line 54, missing DROPLET_HOST/DROPLET_USER/DROPLET_SSH_KEY secrets, or the 12m command_timeout exceeded — would survive the refspec fix. The challenger surfaced this and mitigated it with stage-named ::error instrumentation; the primary has neither a hypothesis nor a fallback.

plan_content.title: Fix failing CI workflow 'Database WAL Archive Freshness' (run #38479376031)

plan_content.architectural_approach: Tier 3 (make it detectable). The defect is undetectability: a monitoring lane that renders verdicts and destroys their proof in the same step. Tier 1 or 2 would require reshaping the payload/output contract, whose consumers (the invariant spec, the resolver script) live beyond this request's allowed scope and are test-pinned — changing them is exactly the correlated blind spot a consumer-first scan exists to catch. Tier 3 is achieved in-file and in-contract: every exit path of the observe and RPO steps carries its evidence (verdict lines plus a bounded tail of the captured payload stdout) into the job log and step summary before the EXIT trap fires, so the wrong behaviour — failing without evidence — is caught and displayed at CI run time in the artifact the verdict lands in.
plan_content.context: What the lane does: every five minutes on main it SSHes to the production droplet through a pinned helper, asks PostgreSQL itself whether archive_mode is on (the only signal that separates the two declared states, per the file's INFRA-CRITICAL-195 comment), runs the in-container WAL-G healthcheck when archiving is present, reconciles the observation against the repo-declared DR capability, and hard-fails on drift in either direction or on an RPO breach. Why this matters: this workflow IS the production backup monitoring — if it fails opaquely, nobody can tell whether production lost WAL archiving or the lane lost its own evidence. What breaks if skipped: the failing run on head 99689e4 stays undiagnosable, and every future failure inherits the same blindness, because the diagnostic artifact is deleted by the cleanup trap before any error message references it. Downstream surfaces: resolve-dr-activation.sh consumes steps.observe.outputs.observed; the activation output gates the RPO step; tests/invariants/wal-archive-activation.spec.ts executes the embedded payload; operators and CI bookkeeping consume the job log as the verdict record. Evidence that proves the result: the only log emissions in the observe step are the cleanup FATAL and the terminal parse error — nothing else in the step writes to the log, which is provable from the file itself.

key_changes.description: Diagnose the failing 'Database WAL Archive Freshness' run on head 99689e46bd86eb980ca2bad74df3c6b072eb4e90 and land the architectural fix in .github/workflows/database-wal-archive-freshness.yml only. Root cause found by reading the file consumer-first: the observe step writes the remote payload's stdout (verdict lines plus the postgres-walg-healthcheck diagnosis) to SSH_STDOUT_PATH inside a mktemp directory guarded by an EXIT trap that rm -rf's it; the step extracts dr_observed/rpo and logs nothing else, so every failure exit (transport failure under set -euo pipefail, the no-recognisable-observation branch, and the RPO-breach error that points at a diagnosis that was never printed) reports a verdict while deleting its proof. The fix makes each exit path emit the captured verdict lines and a bounded tail of the captured stdout into the job log and GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY before the trap fires, without changing any verdict value or the remote payload's output contract.

In the observe step, suspend errexit around the run-protected-ssh.sh invocation, capture its exit status, and — if the stdout capture file exists — print its dr_observed/rpo verdict lines to the job log and step summary before exiting with the captured status. Effect: an SSH/timeout transport failure now states what was observed before the connection died instead of aborting with an empty log.

In the no-recognisable-observation branch, print the bounded raw captured stdout alongside the existing error so the rejected payload output is falsifiable from the log. In the five-minute RPO step, stop pointing operators at a healthcheck diagnosis that lives nowhere in the log: have the observe step write a bounded tail of the captured stdout (the healthcheck's own diagnosis lines) into the step summary and rewrite the breach error to reference that summary section. Keep the remote payload byte-identical — no new output keys, no changed values, no changed exit semantics — because tests/invariants/wal-archive-activation.spec.ts runs this payload (file comment at the observe step) and that spec file is not within the allowed scope, so a payload contract change would leave a broken consumer this plan cannot repair.

Freeze verdict semantics exactly as they are: dr_observed in {present, absent, indeterminate}, rpo in {healthy, breached}, fail-closed resolution in resolve-dr-activation.sh, drift failure in both directions, and the hard fail on RPO breach. The lane's job is to fail when production drifts or breaches; this change adds evidence to failures, never softens a verdict or suppresses a finding.

plan_steps_detailed: Step 1 (observe step, transport path): today set -euo pipefail is active when the pinned run-protected-ssh.sh helper runs, so any nonzero transport exit aborts the step before the awk extraction, and the EXIT trap deletes the capture directory. Restructure: suspend errexit around the helper invocation, record its exit status, print the verdict lines from the capture file to the log and GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY when that file exists, then exit with the recorded status. Cause and effect: transport failures used to leave an empty log; now they leave the last observation on record.

Step 2 (observe step, unparseable path): in the case branch that rejects the observation, print a bounded excerpt (first ~40 lines) of the raw captured stdout next to the existing error before exiting 1. Cause and effect: 'no recognisable observation' becomes checkable — an operator can see what the payload actually said instead of trusting a rejection with no exhibit.

Step 3 (RPO step): the current breach error points at a healthcheck diagnosis that lives only in the capture file the trap deletes. Have the observe step append a bounded tail of the captured stdout to the step summary on the present/breached path, and rewrite the breach error to reference that summary section. Cause and effect: the breach message becomes truthful, and the five-minute-RPO failure is diagnosable from the run alone.

Step 4 (contract freeze): make no change to the remote payload's emitted keys, values, or exit behavior, and no change to the observe step's outputs (observed, rpo) or the activation step's env wiring. Cause and effect: the invariant spec that executes the payload and the resolver that consumes DR_OBSERVED remain green without touching files beyond the allowed scope.
plan_content.recursive_impact: Consumer traversal (reverse of the implementation order): (1) the operator reading a red run consumes the ::error text and job log — currently the error references evidence that is never printed; (2) resolve-dr-activation.sh consumes DR_OBSERVED verbatim — unchanged by this plan; (3) the activation step's dr_verdict output gates the RPO step — unchanged; (4) the invariant spec runs the remote payload — byte-identical after this plan, so the spec stays green by construction rather than by hope; (5) CI bookkeeping that treats lane outcomes as verdicts (the ORPHAN-747 lineage) is unaffected because exit codes and output values are frozen. The only behavior delta is additive log and step-summary lines on failure paths. Coverage closure: a workflow-file change touches no nx project, no libs/event-contracts consumer, and no *.entity.ts, so the computed impact closure has no nodes requiring paths or waivers.

plan_content.summary: The lane is failing on head 99689e46bd86eb980ca2bad74df3c6b072eb4e90 and its own structure makes the failure undiagnosable: the observe step captures the remote payload's stdout — including the WAL-G healthcheck diagnosis — into an umask-077 mktemp directory, extracts only two fields, and the EXIT trap deletes the directory before any failure exit can print what it captured. All three in-file failure exits therefore emit verdicts whose proof never reaches the job log: an SSH transport failure aborts under set -e with the capture deleted, the unparseable-observation error never shows the raw stdout it rejected, and the RPO-breach error says 'See the healthcheck diagnosis above' about text that was provably destroyed. The fix is runner-side only: keep the remote payload's output contract byte-identical (resolve-dr-activation.sh and tests/invariants/wal-archive-activation.spec.ts consume it and are beyond this request's allowed scope) and make every exit path print the verdict lines plus a bounded healthcheck tail into the log and step summary before cleanup fires. This converts the lane from a verdict that destroys its evidence into a self-evidencing detection surface.

Post-merge proof (not a validation command): the lane's next scheduled run (cron */5) must either be green with its verdict lines visible in the log, or red with the diagnosis readable — either outcome satisfies this plan; a red run with a legible cause is a success of the fix and a correct referral to the production owner, not a defect of the lane.

plan_content.architectural_approach: Teaching frame: a CI lane holds three promises — what it reports (verdict), how fast it reports (cadence), and what it holds while reporting (its concurrency slot). This file sets all three to the same number, five minutes, which makes the lane fragile in a specific, mechanical way: any run that consumes its full budget times out red AND still occupies the group's only slot when the next cron mint arrives, so the successor pends and the backlog compounds — the same eviction pathology this lane's history already documented once. The fix is to break the coupling at the budget: shrink per-attempt probe timeout to 60s (the payload's queries are sub-second when the channel is healthy; 60s is generous for connect plus exec), allow exactly one bounded retry for the no-verdict case (a transient docker-exec refusal or a server mid-restart proves nothing either way, per the payload's own comment, and the very next sample answers it), and cap the job at 4 minutes so worst-case occupancy (2x60s + 15s + startup) always releases the slot before the next mint — saturation becomes impossible by construction. That is the automatic tier for the artifact classes. On top of it, the detectable tier: the observe step currently validates only observed and forwards rpo unvalidated, and every downstream failure renders as one anonymous red; the plan validates the rpo channel (healthy/breached required when observed=present) and adds a post-resolution classification step that maps (DR_OBSERVED, dr_verdict) to a named failure class, so drift, breach, indeterminate and channel failures are distinguishable from the log alone — which is also what makes the head failure itself diagnosable after landing. The declared-vs-observed drift gate is never weakened: masking a real drift by widening the indeterminate bucket or softening resolution is prohibited by this plan.
plan_content.context: What this lane is: a five-minute cron that SSH-probes the production droplet, asks PostgreSQL whether archive_mode is on, runs the WAL-G healthcheck when it is, and reconciles the observation against the declared activation state in the checked-out tree; the resolve step fails on drift in both directions by design, and indeterminate observations fail closed. Why it matters: this workflow IS the production RPO monitor — if it wedges or emits unclassifiable reds, operators cannot tell a real archive breach from a CI artifact, and a genuinely unmonitored production database looks identical to a flaky lane. What breaks on head: the file's own numbers couple cadence, budget and slot occupancy (all five minutes), and the observation channel is forwarded without validating rpo; a single stalled hop therefore produces a timeout-red plus a pending successor that later executes a stale probe — and every one of these reds carries the same opaque face. Downstream surfaces: the GitHub scheduler, concurrency group database-wal-archive-freshness-v2, the protected production-backup environment, and the run status operators watch. Evidence: the workflow file itself — cron '*/5 * * * *', timeout-minutes: 5, the concurrency block, the env -i invocation of tools/scripts/ci/run-protected-ssh.sh, the awk parse of stdout with only observed validated, and the resolve/RPO steps that consume its outputs.
plan_content.independence_note: Traversal lens was consumer-first, reverse of implementation-forward: the run's outputs and their consumers (resolve-dr-activation.sh via DR_OBSERVED and dr_verdict; the RPO step via rpo) were read first, then the SSH channel contract (env -i whitelist, stdout file, timeout), then the remote payload, then the scheduling envelope (cron, concurrency, job budget) last. key_changes.description: Diagnose the failing 'Database WAL Archive Freshness' run and land the architectural fix in .github/workflows/database-wal-archive-freshness.yml: set job timeout-minutes to 4, set per-attempt SSH_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS to 60, and wrap the run-protected-ssh.sh invocation in a bounded retry (max 2 attempts, 15s apart) that re-attempts only when an attempt yields no dr_observed verdict (runner nonzero exit, missing stdout file, or observed=indeterminate); after the final attempt without a verdict, emit a classified error annotation naming probe-channel-indeterminate-fail-closed and exit 1. Worst-case in-job time is 2x60s + 15s + startup overhead, strictly under the 4-minute budget, which is strictly under the 5-minute cron cadence — so one run can never still hold concurrency group database-wal-archive-freshness-v2 when its successor is minted, and a transient docker-exec refusal or mid-restart psql read becomes an automatic clean verdict instead of a red. The AQUA_REMOTE_SCRIPT payload heredoc stays byte-identical and the /usr/bin/env -i whitelist passed to tools/scripts/ci/run-protected-ssh.sh stays unchanged.

Close the observation-channel gaps and classify every red in the same file: after parsing stdout, require rpo to be 'healthy' or 'breached' whenever observed=present (a missing or foreign rpo becomes its own classified error instead of an empty GITHUB_OUTPUT line), keep the existing observed/rpo output keys and the DR_CAPABILITY=production-wal-archive value unchanged for the resolve-dr-activation.sh and RPO steps, and add a post-activation summary step that maps the (DR_OBSERVED, steps.activation.outputs.dr_verdict) pair to a named failure class in the run annotation — drift-declared-not-observed, drift-observed-not-declared, probe-indeterminate, rpo-breached, probe-channel-failure — without altering the drift gate or resolve-dr-activation.sh semantics. Each exit path carries an inline comment naming its class and the evidence it reports, so any red run is diagnosable from the log alone.

plan_steps_detailed: 1. Read the failing run's evidence boundary: this envelope carries the workflow file only; the diagnosis therefore enumerates the failure classes the file's own structure produces (timeout on a stalled hop, pending-eviction backlog, single-sample indeterminate fail-closed, unvalidated rpo, genuine drift, genuine RPO breach) and the changes below both remove the artifact classes and label the genuine ones.

2. In the observe step: keep the AQUA_REMOTE_SCRIPT heredoc byte-identical; keep the cleanup trap, umask, and the env -i whitelist exactly; change SSH_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS from 120 to 60 and wrap the single invocation in a loop of at most 2 attempts, 15 seconds apart, where a retry happens only when the attempt produced no dr_observed verdict — runner nonzero exit, missing stdout file, empty observed, or observed=indeterminate. After the final attempt with no verdict, print a classified probe-channel-indeterminate-fail-closed error annotation and exit 1; otherwise proceed with the existing awk parse and observed validation unchanged.

3. Add rpo channel validation in the same step: when observed=present, require rpo in {healthy, breached}; anything else is its own classified error and exit 1, never a silent empty rpo= output line. Keep writing the existing observed and rpo keys to GITHUB_OUTPUT so the activation and RPO steps' input contract is unchanged.

4. Set the verify job's timeout-minutes to 4 (budget strictly below the 5-minute cadence); leave cron '*/5 * * * *', the concurrency group name, cancel-in-progress: false, the main-ref gate, the checkout pin, and the production-backup environment untouched.

5. Add a post-activation summary step (always runs after the activation step, before or after the RPO step) that emits a run annotation naming the failure class from the (DR_OBSERVED, steps.activation.outputs.dr_verdict) pair — drift-declared-not-observed, drift-observed-not-declared, probe-indeterminate, rpo-breached, probe-channel-failure — and add an inline comment at each exit path naming its class. Do not modify the drift gate, the resolve script's invocation, or any step conditionals that implement fail-closed semantics.

6. Verify by diff that the AQUA_REMOTE_SCRIPT payload block is byte-identical to head, that the env -i whitelist is unchanged, and that worst-case occupancy (135s of probe plus startup) fits the 4-minute budget; then run the declared validation commands.

plan_content.summary: The 'Database WAL Archive Freshness' lane couples its schedule (cron */5), its job budget (timeout-minutes: 5) and its single concurrency slot at the same five-minute number, so one slow or stalled SSH probe both burns the entire interval and mints a red that cannot be classified from the run log; the observe step additionally forwards an unvalidated rpo value and turns any single-sample indeterminate into a fail-closed failure. Cause to effect: a stalled hop to the droplet holds concurrency group database-wal-archive-freshness-v2 until the 5-minute timeout kills the job red, the successor mints into a busy group and pends, and pending-duplicate eviction follows — the exact pathology ORPHAN-HIGH-747 documented for this lane's predecessor, re-entering through the -v2 rename. The plan decouples budget from cadence (timeout-minutes 4, per-attempt SSH command timeout 60s, one bounded retry), validates the rpo channel, and gives every remaining failure a machine-readable class, while keeping the AQUA_REMOTE_SCRIPT payload heredoc and every script env/output contract byte-identical. All changes land in the one allowed file.

plan_content.architectural_approach: Tier 1: make the wrong resolution structurally unreachable rather than merely detectable. Reading TARGET_SHA from FETCH_HEAD immediately after the fetch, in the same set -euo pipefail script, with git rev-parse --verify FETCH_HEAD^{commit}, guarantees the SHA is the tip the fetch just wrote: with a configured tracking refspec FETCH_HEAD equals that ref's fresh value; without one, resolution still succeeds instead of aborting or pinning stale state. The alternative — forcing the fetch refspec +refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main — was rejected because it mutates shared refs the deploy control plane also reads, while FETCH_HEAD is private to this invocation and the concurrency group serializes only this workflow. The guarded ::error:: exit additionally converts every early failure in the resolution block from an opaque abort into an annotated step-log line, which is the detectability the next diagnosis will need.
plan_content.context: Teaching frame: this lane is the production droplet's disk-pressure relief valve — the workflow header records that each deploy leaves a prior generation of images untagged and that accumulation blocks the deploy capacity preflight, so a red maintenance lane is a deploy-blocker, not cosmetics. Scan order (independence lens, consumer backward): (1) what consumes the lane — the deploy capacity gate and the droplet-side deploy control plane that consume DEPLOY_SHA and IMAGE_PREFIX; (2) the job envelope — one job (line 54) with exactly one step, the SSH action (line 59), under a 15-minute job timeout, a 12m SSH command timeout, and a single-workflow concurrency group; (3) the remote script, meeting the most recently changed lines last. There the block cd /var/aqua-saas; git fetch --force --prune origin main; TARGET_SHA="$(git rev-parse origin/main)" runs under set -euo pipefail in what the file's own comment calls the persistent bare object store: an explicit-refspec fetch writes FETCH_HEAD and updates refs/remotes/origin/main only when a fetch mapping is configured, so the read fails the run or pins a stale tip. The excerpts were sufficient: all three provided ranges agree line-for-line on their overlaps.

key_changes.description: In .github/workflows/deploy-capacity-maintenance.yml, inside the SSH step's remote script (the sole step, anchored at line 59 of job capacity-maintenance, line 54), replace the line TARGET_SHA="$(git rev-parse origin/main)" with a verified read of the artifact the preceding fetch always writes: if ! TARGET_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify FETCH_HEAD^{commit})"; then echo "::error::Failed to resolve fetched main tip (FETCH_HEAD) in bare store /var/aqua-saas"; exit 2; fi — and keep cd /var/aqua-saas, git fetch --force --prune origin main, export DEPLOY_SHA="${TARGET_SHA}", the deploy-paths.sh bootstrap (git show + source), materialize_deploy_checkout "${TARGET_SHA}", cd "${DEPLOY_CHECKOUT_DIR}", and the OPERATION case dispatch exactly as they are. Root cause treated: in a bare object store, fetching the explicit refspec main updates FETCH_HEAD and only updates refs/remotes/origin/main when a remote.origin.fetch mapping exists, so under set -euo pipefail the current line either aborts the run with an opaque unknown-revision error or silently evaluates a stale commit — the only failure class the file's own text exposes as structurally defective.

Fix (Tier 1): replace the fetch with an explicit destination refspec '+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main' and read 'git rev-parse --verify refs/remotes/origin/main', making the evaluated SHA by construction the tip the fetch just produced; add a 'git cat-file -e "${TARGET_SHA}:scripts/deploy/deploy-paths.sh"' existence guard before the :99 bootstrap that emits a distinct '::error::' annotation and exit code so a missing deploy helper self-identifies instead of surfacing as a bare git-show failure.

plan_content.architectural_approach: Independent traversal order, consumer-backward: I read the droplet-side contract first (what the remote script must provide and call), then the dispatch/scheduler contract (inputs fallback on schedule events, environment, concurrency, timeouts), and the changed remote script last. What that lens exposes: the script's identity guard assumes bash (parameter lowercase expansion, regex conditional) while the workflow never selects the remote shell that executes it; and the script's SHA resolution assumes the bare object store maintains refs/remotes/origin/main, an assumption the file itself flags as a persistent bare store rather than a working tree. The newest change to this file (per derived commit history, orientation only, not evidence) moved both of these into the remote script, and a first-run failure on the current head is most parsimoniously a defect in that delta. The architectural fix is Tier 1 for those two classes: POSIX-only syntax cannot be misparsed by any conformant shell, and FETCH_HEAD cannot be absent after a successful explicit fetch — the wrong behaviour is prevented by construction, not detected after the fact. For the classes the file cannot prevent (genuine capacity verdict, transport/secret failure), the plan's architecture is honest surfacing: classify, fail with the same exit code, and report blocked with the log line — never a weakened gate.
plan_content.context: What this lane is and why a red run matters, in cause-and-effect order: the workflow is the only scheduled janitor for the production droplet's image generations — each deploy pulls ~1.85GB x 13 fresh images and leaves the prior generation untagged, and without the 6-hourly sweep those generations accumulate until the deploy capacity-preflight gate blocks (the #695 failure class the file's own header documents). If this workflow stays red, one of two bad things is true: either the janitor itself is broken and the droplet will refill until deploys block again, or a real capacity signal is being lost inside an undiagnosable failure. Either way the downstream surfaces that break are the deploy-digitalocean preflight (which shares the ghcr.io prefix derivation contract and the checkout bootstrap this step performs), the repository's CI health surface (a red scheduled lane pinned to head 99689e46), and the operator's on-call signal. The evidence that the failure is diagnosable from this file is structural: the job at line 54 contains exactly one step at line 59, whose script block owns every code path between SSH connect and exit.

key_changes.description: Diagnose before editing (mutates no file): pull the failing run's step log and annotations for the single SSH step and classify the failure into exactly one surface this file owns — S1 shell-parse rejection of the remote script's bash-only identity guard (log shows 'Bad substitution' or 'Syntax error' at the IMAGE_PREFIX derivation), S2 target-SHA resolution failure in the bare store (log shows 'unknown revision' or 'ambiguous argument' for origin/main, a fetch auth/network failure, or a missing scripts/deploy/deploy-paths.sh at the resolved SHA), S3 transport surface (secret resolution, appleboy action error, command_timeout 12m exceeded inside timeout-minutes 15), S4 droplet-capacity.sh gate verdict (capacity still below threshold after the bounded GC). The recorded class steers the remaining steps and is quoted in the commit message as the root-cause diagnosis.

Make the remote identity guard structurally shell-agnostic (Tier 1 for class S1): replace the bash-only constructs in the script block — the ${IMAGE_REPOSITORY,,} lowercase expansion and the [[ ... =~ ... ]] regex test — with POSIX-portable equivalents (derive the prefix via printf piped through tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'; validate with a case-glob on ghcr.io/*/* plus per-component character checks accepting components that start [a-z0-9] and continue [a-z0-9._-]*), preserving the identical accepted grammar, the identical error intent, and the identical exit 2 refusal so the INFRA-CRITICAL-085 property that no dispatcher input names an image, registry or repository is unchanged. After this change the guard cannot be a parse error under any remote login shell, because it no longer contains shell-specific syntax.

Anchor target-SHA resolution to the fetch itself (Tier 1 for class S2): in /var/aqua-saas keep 'git fetch --force --prune origin main' but resolve TARGET_SHA via 'git rev-parse --verify FETCH_HEAD' instead of 'git rev-parse origin/main', so resolution cannot depend on refs/remotes/origin/main being configured or current in the persistent bare object store — FETCH_HEAD is written by every successful explicit fetch. Keep the DEPLOY_SHA export, the 'git show ${TARGET_SHA}:scripts/deploy/deploy-paths.sh' bootstrap into /var/lib/aqua/deploy, the source of deploy-paths.sh, materialize_deploy_checkout, and the cd into DEPLOY_CHECKOUT_DIR byte-identical, so the checkout contract shared with the rest of the deploy control plane is untouched.

Make every failure of this lane diagnosable from the run log alone (durably serves the diagnose obligation): capture the capacity invocation's exit status and, immediately before exiting with that same status, echo one greppable terminal line of the form 'capacity-maintenance: class=<S1|S2|S3|S4|gate> stage=<stage> detail=<one-line>'; add the same marker to each early-exit path (identity refusal, fetch/rev-parse/show/bootstrap failures, unsupported operation). Exit codes and gate semantics are unchanged — no '|| true', no softened assertion, no suppressed verdict; only the final log line is added, because appleboy prefixes remote output and ::error:: text from the remote side never renders as a runner annotation.

plan_content.architectural_approach: Tier 3 (make it detectable). Tier 1 is unreachable from the writable surface: the failing contracts bind remote runtime state — the droplet's git store layout, the login shell, the GHCR namespace — which no type system available to a GitHub Actions workflow can structurally constrain. Tier 2 is already spent where it applies: schedule-safe defaults (inputs.* || fallback for OPERATION/FULL_DEPLOY/DEPLOY_SERVICES) and the dispatcher-scope removal (INFRA-CRITICAL-085) already make the correct operation and scope the zero-effort default. What remains is the failure path: each contract boundary becomes an explicit, named check executed before any maintenance action, converting opaque mid-chain 'set -e' aborts into capacity-maintenance:<class> errors and logging the resolved values. For CI infrastructure, run time of the check itself is the build/test-time boundary this tier names; the acceptance signal is that any future red run fails with a named class rather than an opaque abort.
plan_content.context: What must be done and why, as a cause/effect chain: this workflow is the production droplet's only scheduled sweeper (cron '0 */6 * * *') for the untagged image generations every deploy leaves behind (~1.85GB x 13 per deploy, per the workflow's own header); when the lane stays red, nothing sweeps, the droplet climbs past the capacity threshold, and the next production deploy is blocked at capacity preflight — the exact #695 / 28332208818 / 28330781676 class this lane was created to prevent. The red check on head 99689e4 points at the single job (.github/workflows/deploy-capacity-maintenance.yml:54) and its single step (:59), which wraps the whole remote operation in one 'set -euo pipefail' SSH script with no boundary verification: a broken link surfaces as an opaque non-zero exit buried in the log, and a subtly wrong link (for example an IMAGE_PREFIX that passes the regex but no longer matches the producers' namespace) can make the GC a silent no-op while the run stays green. The newest change to this file (8bcacb2519dc, INFRA-CRITICAL-085) rewired two of those links — IMAGE_PREFIX from github.repository and DEPLOY_SHA from the bare store's origin/main — without adding run-time verification. What breaks if skipped: capacity debt re-accumulates until deploys block, and the red lane gives no signal distinguishing an infra-environment fault from a contract fault in the changed code. Downstream surfaces affected: the deploy capacity-preflight gate (consumer of droplet headroom), the GHCR namespace shared with the image producers, and the /var/lib/aqua deploy-checkout namespace shared with the deploy control plane. Evidence proving the result: each boundary emits a named capacity-maintenance:<class> error and the resolved values are logged per run, so the failing contract is identifiable by name from the next run's log; repo-side, the canonical suite proves no collateral breakage.

key_changes.description: Diagnose and fix the failing Deploy Capacity Maintenance check. Root cause as read from the only admissible evidence: the workflow's entire remote operation runs as one 'set -euo pipefail' script behind the single SSH step with zero contract verification, so whichever link breaks — forwarded env vars, bare-store origin/main resolution, the 'git show <sha>:scripts/deploy/deploy-paths.sh' bootstrap, materialize_deploy_checkout/DEPLOY_CHECKOUT_DIR, or the capacity-script path — the run dies as an opaque non-zero exit; the newest commit to this file (8bcacb2519dc) rewired IMAGE_PREFIX (now derived from github.repository) and DEPLOY_SHA (now resolved from the remote's current main) and added no run-time verification for either. Fix, all inside .github/workflows/deploy-capacity-maintenance.yml: (a) assert OPERATION, FULL_DEPLOY, DEPLOY_SERVICES, IMAGE_REPOSITORY are non-empty immediately after 'set -euo pipefail', failing with a named capacity-maintenance:env error; (b) resolve TARGET_SHA with 'git rev-parse --verify' trying refs/remotes/origin/main then refs/heads/main (covers both bare-clone refspecs, which update refs/remotes/origin/main, and mirror-layout stores, which update refs/heads/main directly), failing with a named capacity-maintenance:target-ref error; (c) guard the helper bootstrap with 'git cat-file -e <TARGET_SHA>:scripts/deploy/deploy-paths.sh' before the redirect, failing with capacity-maintenance:bootstrap-helper; (d) after sourcing, assert materialize_deploy_checkout is a declared function ('declare -F'), and after calling it assert DEPLOY_CHECKOUT_DIR is non-empty and an existing directory before 'cd', failing with capacity-maintenance:checkout — this also eliminates the silent cd-to-HOME wrong-directory class when the variable is unset under 'set -u'; (e) assert scripts/deploy/droplet-capacity.sh exists in the checkout before the operation case, failing with capacity-maintenance:capacity-script. Every check prints its error to stderr and exits non-zero before any maintenance or GC action executes. The diff adds no new dispatch input and changes no operation mapping, GC scope, schedule, secret, or concurrency declaration.

Add a per-run diagnosis trail to the same step: echo 'capacity-maintenance:'-prefixed lines for the resolved IMAGE_PREFIX, TARGET_SHA, DEPLOY_CHECKOUT_DIR and OPERATION at each boundary, so the next red run — or a green run whose GC silently matches nothing because the derived prefix drifted from the producers' GHCR namespace — pinpoints the failing contract from the Actions log alone, without droplet SSH access.

In the step's remote script, after 'set -euo pipefail': assert the four forwarded env vars are non-empty; derive and regex-validate IMAGE_PREFIX as today; in /var/aqua-saas, keep 'git fetch --force --prune origin main', then resolve TARGET_SHA via 'git rev-parse --verify' over refs/remotes/origin/main with fallback to refs/heads/main; guard 'git cat-file -e "${TARGET_SHA}:scripts/deploy/deploy-paths.sh"' before the bootstrap redirect; after sourcing, assert 'declare -F materialize_deploy_checkout'; after calling it, assert DEPLOY_CHECKOUT_DIR is non-empty and an existing directory before 'cd'; assert scripts/deploy/droplet-capacity.sh exists before the operation case. Why: every currently-implicit contract becomes a named pre-condition, so the red check self-diagnoses and the silent no-op class (wrong-but-valid prefix, empty checkout var) becomes impossible to miss. Skipped: the lane stays opaque and the deploy-blocking debt class returns.

Why: the Actions log becomes sufficient to adjudicate any future failure without droplet access — the evidence surface moves into the artifact operators already read.

plan_content.recursive_impact: Traversal consumer-to-code, per challenger discipline. (1) Consumer: the production deploy lane's capacity-preflight gate reads droplet disk headroom; this workflow is the only scheduled sweeper, so a red or no-op lane propagates as blocked future deploys, not as repo-code breakage — the #695 / 28332208818 / 28330781676 class named in the workflow's own header. (2) Contract: the GHCR namespace 'ghcr.io/${IMAGE_REPOSITORY,,}' is the shared identity with the image producers (deploy-digitalocean 'prepare' derives the same value, per the workflow's env comment); drift between producer prefix and GC prefix is invisible in a green run and is exactly what the diagnosis trail exposes.
