plan_content.title: Fix failing CI workflow 'CI - Affected' (run #38306753694)

plan_content.architectural_approach: Traversal was consumer-first and backward, per challenger discipline: (1) build-status assertion loop (:2045) — what the operator ultimately sees; (2) merge-gate loop (:2021) — what branch protection sees; (3) the drift between them; (4) the conditional lane jobs docs-check (:1655, :1694), sensor-service-gates, sens-api-gateway-rust (:1761, :1800), sens-enterprise-validation; (5) the core lanes type-check/test (:368 region — the test job's services and its documented 45-minute ceiling); (6) the deploy consumers (:1348, :1363); (7) the head of the file (triggers, detect-changes, install). Two independent findings emerged that a forward implementation-first read anchored on the recently changed lines could miss: the unused-services coupling (visible only when you ask 'what does each job's step body actually reference?') and the consumer-list drift (visible only when you diff the two assert loops side by side). Tier claim: tier 2 — after the change, the decoupled state is the zero-effort default; no author or per-run action is needed for docs-only or Rust-only changes to stop depending on redis/nats availability, and re-coupling would require an explicit new services declaration. Tier 1 (a compiler/runtime that structurally prevents unused service declarations) and tier 3 (a detectable guard, e.g. an invariant spec or workflow-lint script) would both require writing files outside allowed_scope, which this plan will not do.
plan_content.context: What must be done: the workflow 'CI - Affected' is failing on head 99689e46bd86eb980ca2bad74df3c6b072eb4e90, and the obligation is to diagnose the root cause and land an architectural fix touching only .github/workflows/ci-affected.yml. Why it matters: this workflow is the PR and merge-queue gate — branch protection consumes its merge-gate and build-status results, and the main-push deployment lane (development-delivery-status, anchored at :1363) waits behind it. What is actually wrong, from the file alone: every job in the file declares redis+nats service containers, including jobs whose steps never touch ports 6379/4222 (docs-check at :1655/:1694 runs markdownlint only; sens-api-gateway-rust at :1761/:1800 runs cargo audit/check only; merge-gate runs one shell assert loop; install runs npm ci and caches). A service container that fails to pull or pass its health check fails its job — so infrastructure a job never uses can turn the whole run red. Compounding it, the two consumers disagree: the merge-gate loop (anchored at :2021) asserts install/lint/type-check/test/build/pre-flight/infra-image-build-check/security-audit/farm-water-chemistry-e2e/sensor-service-gates/sens-api-gateway-rust/sens-enterprise-validation, while build-status (anchored at :2045) additionally asserts schema-validation, docs-check and sens-enterprise-summary — so a red leg can hide behind a green 'Merge gate passed' message. What breaks if skipped: docs lint, Rust audit, and the merge assert stay coupled to container bootstrap luck, and the next red run is as hard to attribute as this one. Evidence: the service blocks and the complete step lists of the service-free jobs are in the cited excerpts; the assertion-list divergence is visible by comparing the two loops.

key_changes.description: Diagnose and decouple: build a per-job service-reference table by scanning every job's step bodies in .github/workflows/ci-affected.yml for the tokens 6379, 4222, 8222, REDIS, NATS, localhost; delete the redis/nats services blocks only from jobs with zero references. Evidenced service-free jobs: docs-check (checkout, setup-node, global markdownlint install, markdownlint-changed run — no service references), sens-api-gateway-rust (rust toolchain, cargo-audit legs, cargo check — no service references), merge-gate (a single shell assert loop), install (checkout, setup-node, Nx/node_modules caches, npm ci). Keep services on every job with any reference or any test execution: test, sensor-service-gates, sens-enterprise-validation, farm-water-chemistry-e2e.

Unify the two status consumers: add docs-check, schema-validation and sens-enterprise-summary to merge-gate's assertion loop so merge-gate and build-status assert the identical leg set. 'skipped' remains an accepted result in the loop, so conditionally-skipped lanes stay green; the change only makes a failing leg fail both consumers instead of only the final one.

Close the docs-check bootstrap gap: docs-check runs `node scripts/ci/markdownlint-changed.mjs` with no node_modules restore step while its peer jobs restore node_modules from cache. Read scripts/ci/markdownlint-changed.mjs (read-only; the file is not edited) and confirm it imports no workspace modules; if it does import any, add the node_modules cache-restore step (same actions/cache@restore pin already used in the file) to docs-check inside this same workflow file.

plan_steps_detailed: 1. Build the per-job service-reference table from the file itself: for each job in .github/workflows/ci-affected.yml, scan its step bodies (run scripts, env, working-directory, uses inputs) for 6379, 4222, 8222, REDIS, NATS, and localhost. Record each job as service-using or service-free. The four evidenced service-free jobs (docs-check, sens-api-gateway-rust, merge-gate, install) anchor the table; every other job is classified by the same mechanical rule, not by assumption.

2. Delete the redis and nats services blocks from the service-free jobs only. Keep them on test, sensor-service-gates, sens-enterprise-validation, farm-water-chemistry-e2e and any other job the table classifies as service-using (jest/Testcontainers legs connect to 6379/4222 — the services exist there for a reason).

3. Add docs-check, schema-validation and sens-enterprise-summary to merge-gate's assertion loop so it matches build-status's list exactly, preserving the 'skipped'-is-acceptable rule already present in both loops.

4. Read scripts/ci/markdownlint-changed.mjs (read-only; no edit to it — it is not within allowed_scope) to confirm it imports no workspace modules. If it does, add the node_modules cache-restore step to docs-check in this workflow file, mirroring the restore+key pattern sensor-service-gates already uses.

5. Diagnosis reconciliation: compare the failing run's red leg(s) on head 99689e46bd86eb980ca2bad74df3c6b072eb4e90 against the table from step 1 and record the mapping in the PR body — which leg failed, whether it was a service-free job failing on container bootstrap or an attribution mismatch between the consumers. The file-evidenced fix stands on its own; this step proves the diagnosis against the instance and names the leg for the operator.
6. Validate with the declared commands and open the PR against the workflow file only.
plan_content.recursive_impact: Inside the file: removing services from the install job is inert to its outputs (base_sha/has_changes come from detect-changes, not install), so the jobs that need install are unaffected; removing services from docs-check/sens-api-gateway-rust/merge-gate changes only their bootstrap, not their step results. Adding three legs to merge-gate's loop changes merge-gate's verdict only when one of those legs actually fails — the same condition under which build-status already fails the run, so the run-level outcome is unchanged and only attribution becomes consistent. The deploy-lane consumers (deploy-development at :1348, development-delivery-status at :1363, development-timing-summary) gate on different jobs and are untouched. Outside the file: no nx project source, no event contracts, no NATS subscribers, no DB entities or migrations, no frontend modules are modified, so the computed impact closure beyond this file is expected to be empty; the only behavioral ripple is faster, less coupled CI jobs.

risks.mitigation: The step-1 mechanical scan is the gate: any job with any reference token keeps its services; only the four jobs whose complete step lists are in evidence are pre-classified. Jobs with partially visible bodies earn classification only from the scan, never from assumption.
risks.summary: A job classified service-free may reference redis/nats indirectly (e.g. a step reaching localhost:6379 without a literal port token in the visible body).

risks.mitigation: Step 5 reconciles the table against the actual red leg(s) before merge and records the mapping; the failure is immediately visible on the next run either way, and the decoupling fix is independently justified by the file evidence.
risks.summary: The diagnosis is class-level from the file, not log-confirmed: the evidence set contains no run logs, so the specific red leg on the failing head is inferred, and if the actual failure was a genuine code-test failure in a service-using lane this fix removes false-failure modes but not that failure.

risks.mitigation: Intended consequence: build-status already failed the run on those legs, so run-level outcomes are unchanged and attribution becomes consistent; 'skipped' stays accepted so conditional lanes are unaffected.
risks.summary: Adding docs-check/schema-validation/sens-enterprise-summary to merge-gate's loop makes those failures also mark merge-gate red, changing which single check an operator inspects first.

risks.mitigation: Step 4 verifies the script read-only and adds the cache-restore step inside the workflow file only if the script actually imports workspace modules.
risks.summary: docs-check executes scripts/ci/markdownlint-changed.mjs without restoring node_modules, unlike its peer jobs — if the script has workspace imports the job depends on ambient state.

No runtime or persisted state is involved; GitHub Actions picks up the restored definition on the next run. No coordination with any other surface is needed because nothing outside the file changed.
plan_content.summary: The only admissible evidence is the workflow file, so this plan diagnoses the failure family from the file's own structure via a consumer-first traversal (build-status -> merge-gate -> conditional lane jobs -> core lanes -> deploy consumers). Two defects are visible: (1) jobs whose step bodies never reference redis or nats — docs-check, sens-api-gateway-rust, merge-gate, install — still declare both as service containers, so a registry pull or health-check failure in containers nobody uses turns the whole run red; (2) merge-gate and build-status assert different leg sets (merge-gate omits docs-check, schema-validation and sens-enterprise-summary), so a run can fail while merge-gate prints 'Merge gate passed', hiding the red leg from the operator. The fix removes unused services under a mechanical per-job reference rule and unifies the two assertion lists, entirely within the one allowed file. Architectural tier 2 is the highest achievable inside this scope because no compiler or test surface for the workflow file is within allowed_scope.

plan_content.architectural_approach: Tier 2 — make the correct behaviour the zero-effort default, in three moves that each delete a way to be wrong rather than adding a check that catches it later. (1) Lockfile resolution: per-step working-directory is a pin that three sibling steps remember and two forgot; replacing every audit's --file path with a repo-root-qualified path removes the pin itself, so there is no per-step fact left to forget — the path is either right in the file or visibly wrong in review. (2) Gate contract: two hand-maintained copies of the mandatory-jobs list already disagree (merge-gate omits three entries build-status enforces); one workflow-level env list consumed by both loops makes agreement the default and drift a syntax change a reviewer sees in one place. (3) Service containers: declaring Redis/NATS on jobs that never dial a broker is cost with no contract behind it; deleting those blocks makes 'services exist where they are consumed' the structural rule. Tier 1 was considered and rejected honestly: GitHub Actions YAML has no type system that can structurally forbid a relative path or an omitted field, so making the wrong spelling unrepresentable is not available inside this file.
plan_content.context: Teaching frame: 'CI - Affected' is a directed acyclic graph of GitHub Actions jobs. detect-changes computes the base/head range and scope flags; leaf jobs (install, lint, type-check, test, build, schema-validation, docs-check, the sens/farm lanes, the deploy chain on main pushes) each gate one slice; two consumer jobs — merge-gate and build-status, both if: always() — walk explicit lists of needs.<job>.result and fail the check unless every entry is success or skipped. That makes those two loops the workflow's real contract with branch protection: whichever leg goes red, the named error comes from these loops, and the run this plan must fix is leg-named evidence in its own logs. The obligation is to diagnose the failing leg at head 99689e46 and land an architectural fix inside this one file. My traversal ran consumer-to-leaf (the opposite order of a forward implementation read): the assertion loops first, then each leaf job's step list, then the setup jobs. That lens is what surfaces the defect class a forward read skims past — sibling steps that agree on a working-directory except the two that don't.

key_changes.description: Diagnose the failing leg of workflow 'CI - Affected' on head 99689e46 and land the architectural fix in .github/workflows/ci-affected.yml only. Procedure: (1) read the failing run's merge-gate / build-status assertion output — those loops emit '::error::<name> result=<result>' per leg — to name the red job; (2) root suspect from the reverse scan: in the sens-api-gateway-rust job the steps 'Audit alarm-core WASM lockfile' (cargo audit --file crates/alarm-core-wasm/Cargo.lock --deny warnings) and 'Audit protocol-codec WASM lockfile' (cargo audit --file crates/protocol-codec-wasm/Cargo.lock --deny warnings) carry no working-directory, unlike their siblings 'Audit gateway lockfile', 'Audit fuzz lockfile' (both working-directory: sens-api-gateway) and 'Cargo check locked curated CI features' (working-directory: sens-api-gateway), so the WASM audits resolve their lockfile paths from the repo root and cargo-audit fails on a missing file; (3) verify the true lockfile locations read-only (sens-api-gateway/crates/*/Cargo.lock vs a root crates/ tree), then rewrite ALL five audit steps to repo-root-qualified --file paths (for example --file sens-api-gateway/fuzz/Cargo.lock, --file sens-api-gateway/crates/alarm-core-wasm/Cargo.lock) and drop the per-step working-directory from the audit steps, so lockfile resolution can no longer depend on a per-step pin someone can forget; keep every --deny warnings and --ignore RUSTSEC-* flag exactly as-is — no new ignores may be added without a named advisory, because that would suppress a finding rather than fix one.

Close the gate-contract asymmetry between the two result consumers: build-status asserts docs-check, schema-validation, and sens-enterprise-summary must be success-or-skipped, but merge-gate's required-checks loop omits all three, so a red docs or schema leg fails one consumer while the other still prints 'Merge gate passed.' Hoist the mandatory entry list into one workflow-level env variable (a JSON or newline-separated string) and drive BOTH assertion loops from that single source, adding the three missing entries to the enforced set, so the two consumers cannot drift apart again — one list, both loops, no per-job copies.

Delete the redis and nats service blocks from jobs whose shown steps never open a connection to either: docs-check (its steps are checkout, setup-node, global markdownlint-cli install, and node scripts/ci/markdownlint-changed.mjs — markdown linting touches no broker), install (checkout, setup-node, Nx cache, npm ci, node_modules cache save — no service consumer), and sens-api-gateway-rust (checkout, rust toolchain, cargo-audit installs and runs, TPM deps, cargo check — cargo touches no broker). This removes three needless container pulls and health-check waits per run and cuts the mirror rate-limit pressure that INFRA-HIGH-213 chased; keep services on jobs whose tests consume them — the test job and sensor-service-gates (its jest run includes mqtt-listener.service.spec.ts, which is exactly a broker consumer).

plan_steps_detailed: S1 — Name the red leg from the run's own output. Read the failing run's merge-gate and build-status steps: both loops print '::error::<name> result=<result>' for each non-success, non-skipped entry, so the failing job is identified by name in logs the run already produced. Map the name to one of the branches below; every edit in S2-S4 must trace to that named leg or to a defect the file itself proves.

S2 — Fix the cargo-audit lockfile resolution (key_changes[0], the root-cause candidate). Verify read-only where sens-api-gateway's lockfiles actually live (ls sens-api-gateway/crates/*/Cargo.lock, ls sens-api-gateway/fuzz/Cargo.lock). Then rewrite the five audit steps in sens-api-gateway-rust so every --file path is qualified from the repository root (sens-api-gateway/Cargo.lock, sens-api-gateway/fuzz/Cargo.lock, sens-api-gateway/crates/alarm-core-wasm/Cargo.lock, sens-api-gateway/crates/protocol-codec-wasm/Cargo.lock — adjusted to the verified locations) and remove working-directory from the audit steps; the root-lockfile audit stays as a bare cargo audit --deny warnings at the repo root. Preserve every existing --ignore RUSTSEC-* and --deny warnings flag verbatim; adding an ignore without a named advisory is suppression and is not permitted. If the named red leg was sens-api-gateway-rust failing on a missing Cargo.lock, this step is the root-cause fix; if instead an audit leg is red on a real advisory, stop and report blocked — the dependency change that would fix it lives beyond this file's allowed paths.

S3 — Single-source the gate list (key_changes[1]). Add a workflow-level env entry (for example REQUIRED_CHECKS as a JSON array string) listing every mandatory leg — install, lint, type-check, test, build, schema-validation, pre-flight, infra-image-build-check, security-audit, docs-check, farm-water-chemistry-e2e, sensor-service-gates, sens-api-gateway-rust, sens-enterprise-validation, sens-enterprise-summary — and rewrite both the merge-gate loop and the build-status loop to iterate that one variable (build-status keeps its stricter exact-success pass over install/lint/type-check/test/build when has_changes is true). The three entries merge-gate currently omits thereby become enforced by both consumers instead of one.

S4 — Remove dead service containers (key_changes[2]). Delete the redis/nats service blocks from docs-check, install, and sens-api-gateway-rust after re-reading each job's full step list in the file to confirm no step dials a broker; keep the service blocks on test and sensor-service-gates, whose jest runs include broker-consuming specs (mqtt-listener.service.spec.ts). Do not touch the service blocks of any job whose steps were not fully verified in this pass.

S5 — Validate. Run the four canonical commands exactly as declared in validation_commands; then push the branch and confirm the named red leg from S1 re-runs green on a PR, including a merge_group entry if the queue path is exercisable, since merge-gate's contract is what the queue waits on.
plan_content.recursive_impact: The file is a self-contained CI topology; no nx project, event contract, DB entity, or frontend module imports a workflow YAML, so the code-level reverse-dependency closure over this surface is empty and no coverage waivers are claimed. The real dependents are environmental: (a) branch protection and the merge queue — merge-gate listens on merge_group because a workflow that ignored checks_requested would strand queued entries; any edit that changes which legs are asserted changes what may merge, which is exactly what key change 2 tightens deliberately; (b) the development deploy chain (deploy-development, development-delivery-status, development-timing-summary) — untouched by this plan, and deliberately so: the operator-owned DEVELOPMENT_DEPLOY_MODE hold design is a decided prior outcome, and this plan re-litigates none of it; (c) the weekly ci-full lane, whose test-job budget of 45 minutes bounds this file's test ceiling from above through tests/invariants/ci-timeout-budget-ssot.spec.ts — a constraint this plan respects by not raising the ceiling.

risks.mitigation: The implementer reports blocked with the dependency files as enabling surfaces instead of adding an undocumented --ignore; suppressing the advisory inside the workflow would trade a red check for an unmitigated vulnerability, which this plan's discipline forbids.
risks.summary: If the named red leg is a cargo audit going red on a real advisory (the root-lockfile audit runs --deny warnings with no exception list, unlike the gateway audit's four documented RUSTSEC ignores), the honest fix is a dependency bump or a reviewed ignore — and both live beyond this file's allowed paths.

risks.mitigation: S2 gates the edit on a read-only location check, and the rewrite to root-qualified paths is correct under either layout — only the diagnosis narrative changes, never the edit's validity. S1's leg-naming procedure keeps the plan anchored to the run's own failure signal rather than to this hypothesis.
risks.summary: The crates/ location hypothesis could be wrong: if the repository root genuinely hosts a crates/alarm-core-wasm tree, the two WASM audits resolve correctly today and the root cause lies in a different leg.

risks.mitigation: Keep the loop bodies mechanically identical to today's (same name:result parsing, same success/skipped rule), change only the source of the list; verify on a PR branch that a deliberately-skipped leg (for example docs-check on a code-only change) is accepted and a failing leg is named — proving the indirection preserves the semantics before it guards merges.
risks.summary: Single-sourcing the gate list through workflow env changes the merge-gate contract from a literal list to an indirected one, and quoting or expansion mistakes in the loop could fail every PR at once.

risks.mitigation: S4 requires re-reading each job's complete step list in the file before deleting its services, and only the three jobs whose steps are enumerated here are candidates; any job whose steps were not fully inspected keeps its services untouched.
risks.summary: Deleting service containers from a job that silently depended on one would turn a green job red in a different way; the shown step lists for docs-check, install, and sens-api-gateway-rust contain no broker consumer, but the file is long and excerpts are windows.

risks.mitigation: This plan does not raise the ceiling; if S1 names the test job as the red leg on a timeout, the in-file responses are step-budget reduction or splitting the overloaded step, and the ceiling stays at the invariant-bounded 45.
risks.summary: The test job's 45-minute ceiling sits over step budgets that sum to 140 minutes, so a broad affected set can time the job out; raising the ceiling above 45 would violate the ci-timeout-budget invariant unless ci-full.yml rose with it, and that file is not in this plan's allowed paths.

plan_content.rollback: The change is one declarative file. Rollback is a single-file git revert of the implementing commit; no runtime state, no migrations, no emitted events, and no deploy behavior is touched (the development-deploy chain is unmodified). Because key change 2 only widens which legs merge-gate asserts, a revert restores the previous assertion set without leaving any half-applied contract; because key changes 1 and 3 delete rather than transform, reverting restores the exact prior job definitions byte-for-byte.
plan_content.summary: Read as a junior engineer would: this workflow is a chain of leaf jobs whose results are consumed by two assertion jobs, merge-gate and build-status; any red leaf turns the required check red and blocks every PR, so a failing run must map to exactly one named leg, and the assertion loops themselves print that name. My independent reverse scan (consumers first, changed code last) finds the strongest file-visible defect inside the sens-api-gateway-rust job: 'Audit alarm-core WASM lockfile' and 'Audit protocol-codec WASM lockfile' reference crates/*/Cargo.lock with no working-directory, while the gateway audit, fuzz audit, and cargo check all pin working-directory: sens-api-gateway, so the WASM audits resolve their lockfiles against the repo root where those paths do not exist. The same scan surfaces two sibling defects on the same file: merge-gate's required-checks loop omits docs-check, schema-validation, and sens-enterprise-summary that build-status enforces, and docs-check, install, and sens-api-gateway-rust declare Redis/NATS service containers their shown steps never use. All edits stay inside .github/workflows/ci-affected.yml at architectural tier 2: correct behaviour becomes the zero-effort default (repo-root-qualified lockfile paths, one shared gate list, services only where consumed).

plan_content.validation_plan: Primary: the four operator-declared commands — npx nx affected --target=test (the affected suite includes the CI-budget invariant spec that reads this file and pins the test-job ceiling to the ci-full SSOT), npx nx affected --target=lint, npm run type-check (regression guard even though no TS changes), and node tools/quality/quality.mjs format check-changed (the enforced format gate over the edited YAML). Success criterion beyond exit 0: the leg named in S1 re-runs green on a PR branch, and both merge-gate and build-status print 'Merge gate passed.' / exit 0 with the shared list — proving the two consumers now agree by construction rather than by inspection. For S2 specifically, the corrected audit steps must run against lockfiles that exist at the resolved path; a file-not-found after the rewrite means the location verification in S2 was wrong, not that an ignore should be added.

risks.recommendation: Fold the challenger's lockfile-resolution fix into the primary's key changes: verify read-only where sens-api-gateway's WASM lockfiles actually live, rewrite the two working-directory-less audit steps to repo-root-qualified --file paths, and widen key-change-004's reconciliation from 'the test leg' to 'the named red leg read from the run's own ::error:: output'.
risks.summary: The primary plan never surfaces the strongest file-visible root-cause candidate: in sens-api-gateway-rust the two WASM audit steps run 'cargo audit --file crates/*/Cargo.lock' with no working-directory while their sibling steps pin working-directory: sens-api-gateway, so those lockfile paths resolve from the repo root — if that job is the red leg of run #38306753694, the primary's service-decoupling and gate-list fixes leave the run red and its key-change-004 reconciliation (which examines only the test leg) never checks it.

risks.recommendation: Make the named-leg diagnosis (the challenger's S1 procedure — both consumer loops print '::error::<name> result=<result>' per red leg) a recorded precondition in the PR body before any edit lands, and require every mechanical edit to trace to that named leg or to a defect the file itself proves.
risks.summary: Neither plan carries run-log evidence naming the red leg of run #38306753694 — both interleave diagnosis and fix inside one PR, and each names a different hypothesis (primary: service-bootstrap failure on the test leg; challenger: cargo-audit lockfile resolution) — so if the actual red leg is one neither branch covers (e.g. a real RUSTSEC advisory on the root lockfile, the npm audit gate, or a deploy-chain leg), the landed edits are unvalidated against the failure the obligation requires diagnosed.

plan_content.architectural_approach: Tier 2 — make the correct behaviour automatic. After the change, waiver-channel visibility requires zero contributor or automation effort on every event class the workflow triggers: pull_request runs read the body directly, push runs resolve the associated merged PR's body from the commit SHA via the GitHub API. Tier 1 (structurally impossible via types/compiler) is not reachable from inside the workflow file because the PR-body dependence lives in the invariant spec, which is outside this plan's allowed surface. The rejected alternative — restricting invariants-fast to pull_request events only — was rejected on tier grounds: it removes detection coverage on push runs, which is a detection downgrade of exactly the class the file's own header says these gates exist to prevent ('Making it a required job means the next drift breaks the PR, not the next audit'). Direct pushes with no associated PR deliberately resolve to an empty body: the invariant then enforces the unwaived path, which is the gate's designed behaviour, not a regression.
plan_content.context: What must be done and why, for a junior engineer reading this plan cold. The Quality Gates workflow is red on head f2506ac8f56b11a078bfc5104488ff0258a9acc0 and the fix may touch only the workflow file itself. Read the file backward, from what consumes it: (1) the Jest invariant suite consumes an env contract PR_BODY — the workflow's own comment on the final invariants-fast step states that entity-diff-implies-migration.spec.ts honours 'ENTITY-DIFF-OK:' PR-body waivers via PR_BODY and that 'without this env the invariant cannot see the waiver and fails any entity edit that has no accompanying migration'; (2) the only producer of PR_BODY in the file is the static mapping PR_BODY: github.event.pull_request.body; (3) that context object exists only when the event is pull_request, yet the workflow's on: block also fires on push to main/develop. Cause/effect chain: push-class run → pull_request context absent → PR_BODY empty → waiver invisible → invariant fails an entity edit that was legitimately waived in its PR body → Quality Gates red on the push run even though the PR run was green. What breaks if skipped: every merge containing a waived entity-typing change turns the workflow red on main/develop, training contributors to ignore a required gate. Evidence that proves the result: the next push-event run of the workflow passes invariants-fast with the resolution step in place; the four canonical validation commands prove the edit itself is format-clean and breaks no build surface.

key_changes.description: Failing CI workflow 'Quality Gates' (.github/workflows/quality-gates.yml) on head f2506ac8f56b11a078bfc5104488ff0258a9acc0; diagnose root cause + land architectural fix. Diagnosed root cause from the workflow's own structure: the invariants-fast job resolves the entity-diff-witness waiver input PR_BODY exclusively from github.event.pull_request.body in its final step's env block, an input that exists only on pull_request events, while the workflow's on: block also triggers push to main/develop — so on push-class runs the waiver channel is structurally empty and entity-diff-implies-migration fails any entity edit whose waiver lived in the merged PR body.

In .github/workflows/quality-gates.yml, add a 'Resolve PR body (event-class independent)' step immediately before the 'Run Jest invariants' step: on pull_request events export github.event.pull_request.body to PR_BODY; on all other events resolve the associated merged pull request via gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{github.sha}/pulls (GH_TOKEN from github.token) and export its body, resolving to an empty string only when no associated PR exists (direct pushes keep the unwaived enforcement path, which is the gate working as designed; real API errors fail the step loudly). Remove the static PR_BODY mapping from the Jest step so the resolution step is the single source of truth, add pull-requests: read alongside the existing contents: read in the top-level permissions block, and update the job's comment block to record the root cause and the resolution contract.

plan_steps_detailed: Confirm the diagnosis against the failing run before editing: verify the red lane on head f2506ac8f56b11a078bfc5104488ff0258a9acc0 is the invariants-fast job and the run is push-class (pull_request context absent). If the red lane is a different job or the failure text points at a red invariant spec rather than the waiver channel, stop and surface a blocked verdict — the fix surface would then sit outside the allowed scope of this plan.
Edit the top-level permissions block: keep contents: read, add pull-requests: read so the associated-PR lookup works under least privilege.

Insert a 'Resolve PR body (event-class independent)' step before the 'Run Jest invariants' step: on pull_request, export the event's body; otherwise call gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{github.sha}/pulls with GH_TOKEN from github.token, select the merged PR associated with the SHA, export its body; export an empty string only when the returned list is empty. Fail the step on real API errors rather than swallowing them. Use a safe multi-line delimiter (or a temp file re-read into the env) so PR bodies containing arbitrary text cannot break the export.
Delete the static PR_BODY mapping from the 'Run Jest invariants' step env block so the resolution step is the single producer of PR_BODY for both event classes.
Update the invariants-fast comment block to record the root cause (push-event blindness of a pull_request-only input) and the new resolution contract, in the file's existing comment discipline.

Run the four canonical validation commands, then open the fix PR; the operative proof is the push-event run of Quality Gates on the merge of that PR passing invariants-fast where it previously failed.
plan_content.recursive_impact: Consumer-backward closure over the only admissible file. Direct consumers of the changed lines: (a) the entity-diff-witness gate inside the Jest invariant suite, whose waiver input contract (PR_BODY text) becomes available on both event classes instead of one; (b) the GitHub checks UI, which gains one resolution step in the invariants-fast lane — the file's own comment discipline says lanes are kept separately so gate-CLI and invariant-spec changes surface in independently-retryable lanes, and this change stays inside the invariants-fast lane. Indirect consumers: branch protection on main/develop that requires Quality Gates, and every push/PR to those branches (the on: block). No Nx project graph node, NATS event contract, entity, or migration surface is touched by a YAML-only edit to this workflow, so the computed impact closure beyond the file itself is empty and no coverage waiver is needed.

plan_content.summary: An independent backward scan (consumer and contract end first, changed file last) of the Quality Gates workflow identifies the invariants-fast job — the request's anchored line 205 — as the failing surface. The job feeds the entity-diff-witness waiver channel (PR_BODY) from github.event.pull_request.body, which is structurally empty on the push-event runs that the same workflow's on: block triggers, so an entity change merged under an ENTITY-DIFF-OK waiver passes its PR run and re-fails the push run of Quality Gates. The plan lands a tier-2 architectural fix entirely inside the workflow: an event-class-independent PR-body resolution step plus a least-privilege pull-requests: read grant, keeping the invariant hard gate active on both event classes rather than narrowing when it runs.

plan_content.architectural_approach: Tier 2 — make the correct behaviour the zero-effort default. Today the waiver channel exists only when a pull_request payload happens to be present; after the change it is populated on both trigger types with no contributor action: the PR body on pull_request runs, the push's head commit message on push runs. This repo already treats the commit message as the durable carrier of PR-body content (trailer-bearing merge convention), so the channel survives the event boundary that broke it. Tier 1 was considered and rejected honestly: no YAML expression can structurally guarantee that a waiver exists when the pushed content genuinely lacks one — and that residual failure is the invariant performing its designed function, not a defect to engineer away. plan_content.architectural_approach: Tier 1 for the headline repair: deleting a services block removes the failure path structurally - the Actions runtime cannot fail a job on a container it was never asked to start, so no later lint rule or test is needed to catch the wrong behaviour. The same deletion removes wasted container startup on every PR for jobs that never connected. The secondary repair (merge-gate assertion alignment) is tier 3 for its own defect class: the wrong state - merge-gate green while a build-status-required job is red - becomes detectable by the gate itself once both loops assert the identical set. Diagnosis precedes the edit because the admissible evidence contains the workflow but not the failing run's log: this store rejects run-log citations (the recorded rejection of the prior challenger attempt on claim_45ff1db73bdba795 cites exactly that), so the implementer reads the run during implementation, and the structural repairs stand on their own excerpt-verified evidence regardless of which class the specific run falls into.
plan_content.context: What is failing and why it matters: the 'CI - Affected' workflow is red on head be8f1d1c86c131309d9e112b65f9e42188f2aee4, and every PR, merge-group entry, and push to main waits on it - build-status asserts every job's result (.github/workflows/ci-affected.yml:2046) and its needs list (.github/workflows/ci-affected.yml:2022) defines what 'green' means - so a red run here blocks all delivery, not one job. How to read it, backwards from the consumer as the challenger does: each asserted job name points at a producer job; the producer's own definition shows whether its failure can be self-inflicted or infra-inflicted. What the backward read finds: install, docs-check (.github/workflows/ci-affected.yml:1655 region), and merge-gate declare redis and nats service containers, yet their complete step lists (npm ci plus caches; markdownlint; a bash result-assertion) never connect to ports 6379 or 4222. In GitHub Actions a service container is a hard job dependency: if the image pull stalls, the job is red before its first step, so a markdownlint job can fail on a registry outage it never needed. The registry was already moved once (every services block pulls from the public.ecr.aws mirror per the excerpts) precisely because of a prior rate-limit incident class in this repository's history; the fix changed the registry, not the exposure - every unused declaration survived it. What breaks if skipped: hermetic jobs keep carrying a standing failure channel and the next registry incident reds build-status again through no fault of any step. Evidence that proves the result: the three jobs' complete step lists are visible in the excerpts (no service consumer exists in them), and after the fix the next CI - Affected run shows those jobs starting with no service containers and build-status green.

key_changes.description: Diagnose the failing 'CI - Affected' run on head be8f1d1c86c131309d9e112b65f9e42188f2aee4 and land the architectural fix inside .github/workflows/ci-affected.yml only: read the failing job and step from the run's log and classify it - (a) service-container startup/health failure in a job whose steps never connect to redis (6379) or nats (4222), (b) a step's own logic, (c) a result-assertion gate. The evidence-verified structural repair for class (a), applied regardless as it stands on its own excerpt evidence: delete the services: block from every job whose full step list never opens 6379/4222 - install, docs-check, and merge-gate are deletion-verified from the evidence excerpts because their complete step lists are visible; lint, type-check, test, and sensor-service-gates are inspect-first (read each job's entire step list for 6379/4222/REDIS/NATS/localhost usage) and keep their services where any step genuinely connects.

Close the assertion drift between the two result gates: build-status's first assertion loop requires schema-validation, docs-check, and sens-enterprise-summary to be success-or-skipped, but merge-gate's 'Assert required PR checks' loop omits all three, so the merge-blocking gate can pass while a job build-status treats as required is red. Add the three missing entries to merge-gate's loop and the matching needs: entries if absent, so both gates assert one identical required set.

plan_content.architectural_approach: Tier claim: 1, disclosed per change. The docs-check service deletion makes that failure class structurally impossible: a job that declares no service containers cannot fail on a registry pull or a health check - the job runner itself prevents it (tier 1, achieved by deleting a surface, not by adding a guard). The ceiling re-derivation, when the diagnosis names the test leg, rides an existing tier-3 control: tests/invariants/ci-timeout-budget-ssot.spec.ts fails the test lane on any budget that breaks the SSOT relation. The plan adds no new guard machinery; it deletes one failure surface and re-aligns one number with an invariant the repository already owns.
plan_content.context: Run 38744002589 (id carried by the obligation's key_change_id) left 'CI - Affected' red on head be8f1d1c. Why that matters: this workflow is the PR and merge-queue gate. Merge-gate and build-status consume every leg's needs.*.result and convert any non-success, non-skipped value into a failed run, so one red leg blocks every queued PR. The challenger scan ran consumer-first (the reverse of the changed-code-forward reading): assertion jobs (2022, 2046), then job bodies (docs-check 1655/1694, test 368, delivery chain 1348/1363), then the detect-changes contract at the top of the file. Two failure surfaces can turn the run red with no code defect, and both are repairable within allowed_scope: (a) docs-check declares redis and nats service containers that none of its steps touch - a markdown gate that can fail on infrastructure before lint ever runs; (b) the test job's 45-minute ceiling is a copied measurement ('median 23m29s, max 29m03s' per the in-file comment) whose drift is caught only by tests/invariants/ci-timeout-budget-ssot.spec.ts.

key_changes.description: Diagnose the red leg of the failing 'CI - Affected' run on head be8f1d1c from the workflow's own assertion output - merge-gate's result loop (line 2022 region) and build-status's loop (line 2046 region) print the failing job's name and result - then land the architectural fix for that leg with edits confined to .github/workflows/ci-affected.yml. If the named leg is neither docs-check nor test (for example the security-audit npm legs), the fix surface is not in this file and the implementer refuses with the enabling surfaces named.

Delete the redis and nats service-container declarations from the docs-check job (job at line 1655; its steps - checkout, setup-node, global markdownlint-cli install, markdownlint-changed at line 1694 - consume no service), so a markdown lint gate can no longer fail on a container-registry pull or a service health check before any step runs.

If and only if kc-0 names the test leg: re-derive the test job's timeout-minutes (test job at line 368; the ceiling and its SSOT comment sit inside the job) from ci-full.yml's current budget, keeping the filtered lane at or below the unfiltered lane so tests/invariants/ci-timeout-budget-ssot.spec.ts verifies the relation under the test lane.

Preserve every job id and the success/skipped result contract that merge-gate (line 2022) and build-status (line 2046) consume; branch protection and the merge queue key required checks to these names, so the change touches job internals only and renames nothing.

plan_steps_detailed: Read the failure where the workflow itself records it. The assertion jobs are the consumers of every leg result: merge-gate's loop (line 2022 region) and build-status's loop (line 2046 region) print '::error::<job> result=<value>' naming the red leg. Effect: the diagnosis is derived from the run's own output; skipping this step risks repairing a leg that did not fail.

Map the named leg to one of the two in-file failure surfaces the independent scan identified: docs-check (job at 1655, markdownlint step at 1694) or test (job at 368). If the leg is neither - for instance the security-audit npm audit legs or the gateway audit exception - stop and emit an implementation refusal naming the enabling surfaces, because the fix for those legs does not live in this file.

Delete the redis and nats service declarations from docs-check. Cause and effect: the job's steps (checkout, setup-node, global markdownlint-cli install, markdownlint-changed) touch no service; today a registry pull failure or an unhealthy container reds a markdown gate before any step runs; after the deletion that failure class cannot occur because there is no service to fail.

If the named leg is test: read ci-full.yml's current test budget (read-only), set this job's timeout-minutes to the SSOT-consistent value, and let the invariant spec verify the relation under the test lane. Cause and effect: a ceiling below real runtime kills green code; a ceiling above the unfiltered lane's budget is a contradiction the spec rejects.

Rename nothing. Branch protection and the merge queue (the workflow's on: merge_group trigger) key required checks to the current job names; a rename leaves queued entries waiting until the queue times out.

Run the declared canonical commands, then treat the next 'CI - Affected' run on the fix PR as the operative end-to-end proof: docs-check green with no service containers, merge-gate and build-status assertions passing.
recursive_impact: merge-gate (line 2022 region) and build-status (line 2046 region): consumers of every leg result. The fixes keep job ids and the success/skipped contract unchanged, so the assertion loops need no edits and continue to function identically.

Branch protection and the merge queue: the workflow listens on merge_group so queued entries request these exact check names. No job is renamed, so required-check mappings and queue behavior are untouched by both the change and its rollback.

development-delivery-status (line 1348) and its 'Require successful development delivery' step (line 1363): surveyed consumer-first. The held-mode exemption is coherent - a hold is a declared state with built images, every other mode must have deployed. No defect found; no change prescribed (stated explicitly rather than by silence).
The weekly ci-full lane: bounds the ceiling re-derivation through the SSOT invariant spec; the filtered <= unfiltered relation is machine-checked by the test lane, not by prose.
merge-gate's loop omits docs-check while build-status's loop includes it: surveyed as deliberate layering (merge-gate asserts the PR-required set, build-status asserts the whole run). No change.

If the red leg is instead the security-audit npm legs (1615-1633 region) or the gateway audit exception, no fix surface exists within allowed_scope.

plan_content.validation_plan: npx nx affected --target=test runs tests/invariants/ci-timeout-budget-ssot.spec.ts (named inside the test job's own comment, cited at line 368), which machine-checks the timeout SSOT relation the ceiling change must satisfy, and runs the affected suite as the regression net for the workflow edit. npx nx affected --target=lint and npm run type-check prove the workspace still lints and compiles (no TS is touched; they are the floor, not the target). node tools/quality/quality.mjs format check-changed is the enforced format gate covering the edited YAML. The operative downstream proof, observed rather than declared: the next 'CI - Affected' run on the fix PR must be green with docs-check reporting no service containers and both assertion loops passing.

risks.recommendation: Gate kc-p-003's needs/loop additions on the branch-protection confirmation arriving BEFORE the edit (operator confirmation or an operator-supplied admissible ref), and keep the always() verification-plus-extension in the same commit as the needs additions so the gate can never skip on a skipped conditional need.
risks.summary: Primary lands the merge-gate alignment edit unconditionally while both its necessity and its safety rest on out-of-repo branch protection it cannot verify: the operator confirmation in R-P-003 is requested after the edit lands, and merge-gate's job-level if: condition is not visible in the evidence, so a missed always() extension alongside new needs entries for conditional jobs (docs-check runs only when docs_changed) can leave a required check skipped and merge-queue entries stranded — the gate the primary itself names the most extreme affected node.

risks.recommendation: Add a conditional ceiling branch mirroring kc-2: if the pinned diagnosis shows a timeout kill of the test job, re-derive timeout-minutes against the ci-full budget and let the SSOT invariant spec verify the relation under the test lane.
risks.summary: Primary has no repair branch for a test-leg failure whose in-file cause is the timeout ceiling: timeout-minutes sits inside the allowed file, and the job's own comment documents both the ci-full SSOT bound and the invariant spec that machine-checks the relation — yet the (a)/(b)/(c) classification routes every test-leg cause to either the service audit or a blocked report, never to the ceiling re-derivation the challenger carries as kc-2.

plan_content.title: Fix failing CI workflow 'CI - Affected' (run #38744002589)

plan_content.architectural_approach: Tier 1 for the class it targets: a job that declares no service container cannot fail on that service's image pull or health check, so removing the dead Redis/NATS blocks from service-independent gate jobs makes their infrastructure-coupled red structurally impossible rather than merely detected. The diagnosis method is the mirror of the file's own control flow: build-status and merge-gate only aggregate needs.*.result strings, so the true red always sits exactly one hop upstream of the red face, and the gate loops enumerate the candidate set without run logs. Removal is gated on proof (a job's complete step list showing no service consumption) rather than on suspicion, which is why test (368) and sensor-service-gates (1694) are excluded from removal by default — the test job hosts the integration lane whose Testcontainers steps the file's own comments document, and sensor-service-gates' body is only partially visible in evidence.
plan_content.context: The workflow triggers on push to main, pull requests to main and merge_group, resolves an immutable affected range in detect-changes, and fans out to lane jobs aggregated by merge-gate and build-status; the failed run (candidate id ci-run-38744002589) is red at head be8f1d1. The allowed fix surface is the workflow file alone, which itself constrains the root cause to workflow structure or workflow-to-infrastructure coupling rather than application code. Reading order for this plan was consumer-backward: build-status (2022/2046) and merge-gate first, then the lanes they assert (docs-check 1655, sensor-service-gates 1694, test 368, the development delivery chain 1348/1363), then job bodies last.

key_changes.description: Diagnose the failing CI workflow 'CI - Affected' (.github/workflows/ci-affected.yml) on head be8f1d1c86c131309d9e112b65f9e42188f2aee4 and land the architectural fix: enumerate which lane jobs can red the run through build-status (line 2046 asserts schema-validation, docs-check, sensor-service-gates, sens-* lanes as success-or-skipped and install/lint/type-check/test/build as strict success when has_changes=true) and merge-gate (whose loop omits docs-check, schema-validation and sens-enterprise-summary), then remove the Redis/NATS service-container coupling from every job whose complete step list provably never uses those services, starting with docs-check.

Delete the redis and nats services blocks from the docs-check job: its entire step set is visible in the evidence (actions/checkout, actions/setup-node, 'npm install -g markdownlint-cli@0.45.0', 'node scripts/ci/markdownlint-changed.mjs' with MARKDOWNLINT_BASE_REF/HEAD_REF env) and references neither port 6379 nor 4222 nor any Redis/NATS client, so a docs-only change can currently fail CI purely on service image pull or health, propagating red through build-status at line 2046.

For each remaining job in the file, verify service usage from that job's own complete step list (search its run blocks and env for 6379, 4222, REDIS, NATS, localhost and any client invocation) and delete its services blocks only where non-use is proven by those steps; keep the services on test (line 368, which hosts the Testcontainers integration lane) and on sensor-service-gates (line 1694) unless their steps prove otherwise, and do not touch jobs whose bodies are not verifiable from the file.

While editing, verify the two aggregate gates remain internally consistent after the change: build-status (line 2022) must still list and assert docs-check, and the development chain (development-delivery-status at lines 1348/1363, deploy-development feeding it) must be unaffected because the edit removes no job, no needs edge and no condition — the diff must show only services-block deletions.

plan_steps_detailed: 1. Backward pass: from build-status (2022/2046) and the merge-gate loop, list every lane whose result string can redden the run; this enumerates the candidate red jobs for run 38744002589 on head be8f1d1 without logs.

2. Proven-instance fix: delete the redis and nats services blocks from docs-check; its whole step list (checkout, setup-node, markdownlint-cli global install, markdownlint-changed.mjs with only MARKDOWNLINT_* env) is visible and service-free.

3. Conditional same-class fix: for each other job, inspect that job's own steps for any service consumption (6379/4222/REDIS/NATS/localhost/client usage); delete services blocks only on proof of non-use; leave test and sensor-service-gates in place absent that proof.

4. Consistency check in the same edit: diff contains only services-block deletions in .github/workflows/ci-affected.yml; build-status still lists and asserts docs-check; the development chain (1348-1380) is byte-identical.

5. Verify the documented timeout invariant still holds while in the file: the comment block above the test job (around 368-395) states tests/invariants/ci-timeout-budget-ssot.spec.ts requires ci-full's unfiltered test budget to be at least this workflow's 45; confirm ci-full's current value still satisfies it (verification read only; adjust this file's ceiling only if the invariant demands it, which is an in-scope edit).
plan_content.recursive_impact: No nx project owns .github paths, no event-contract or entity/migration surface is touched, and nothing imports the workflow file, so the computed impact closure is expected to be empty and no coverage waivers are claimed. The human-facing consumers are the branch-protection required checks (build-status runs if: always() and is the run-level red face; merge-gate asserts the PR lanes), the merge queue (the merge_group trigger exists precisely so queued entries do not stall), and the development deploy chain: deploy-development (called with outputs of build-development-images) and development-delivery-status (1348/1363), which require upstream success and whose behavior is unchanged because the edit deletes no job, needs edge, output or condition.

risks.mitigation: Step 1's backward gate-walk plus the run's per-check results on head be8f1d1 identify the red lane before editing; if the red lane is one this plan's evidence cannot explain, that fact is reported rather than papered over.
risks.summary: The specific red lane of run 38744002589 is not identifiable from the workflow file alone; if the red came from a cause other than service-container coupling (for example a genuine test failure in the test job at line 368), the decoupling fix eliminates the proven dead-coupling class but does not repair that specific red.

risks.mitigation: Removal is gated on that job's complete step list showing zero service consumption; test (368) and sensor-service-gates (1694) are excluded from removal by default, and the validation suite runs against the changed file.
risks.summary: Deleting a services block from a job that consumes Redis/NATS through indirect env or a script would break that lane at runtime even though the workflow parses.

risks.mitigation: Record the asymmetry; build-status (2022, if: always()) currently asserts the full set and is the run-level authority; any change to the split needs branch-protection evidence this request does not carry.
risks.summary: merge-gate's checked loop omits docs-check, schema-validation and sens-enterprise-summary (only build-status asserts those), so if branch protection required merge-gate without build-status, a red docs-check could pass the queue gate; this plan does not change that split because no evidence proves a protection-rule defect.

risks.mitigation: Step 5 verifies the relation as part of the diagnosis pass; if inverted, lowering this file's ceiling is an in-scope edit that restores the invariant.
risks.summary: The timeout-budget SSOT documented in the test-job comment (tests/invariants/ci-timeout-budget-ssot.spec.ts requiring ci-full's unfiltered budget >= this workflow's 45) could have been inverted by the recent CI-Full budget re-derivation, which would redden the test lane independently of services.

plan_content.rollback: Single-file revert: git revert of the one commit restoring the deleted services blocks. The change carries no state, schema, migration or data impact; no job graph edge is added or removed, so the pre-change behavior returns exactly, including the pre-change (coupled) failure mode. No other surface needs coordinated rollback because nothing outside .github/workflows/ci-affected.yml is touched.
plan_content.summary: The failed 'CI - Affected' run on head be8f1d1 surfaces through the aggregate gates (build-status asserts every lane at line 2046), so this plan walks the gate graph backward from build-status and merge-gate to the lane jobs instead of reading the file forward. The one defect the scan proves from the file itself: docs-check (line 1655) declares Redis and NATS service containers while its complete visible step list — checkout, setup-node, global markdownlint-cli install, scripts/ci/markdownlint-changed.mjs — never connects to either port, coupling a pure documentation gate to container-registry and service-container health, the exact external-dependency class that already took this workflow down repeatedly (INFRA-HIGH-213 DockerHub rate limiting, mitigated by the ECR-mirror commit in recent intent). The fix removes service blocks only where a job's full step list proves non-use — docs-check first; test (line 368) and sensor-service-gates (line 1694) stay untouched unless their own steps prove otherwise — which makes the dead-service failure class structurally impossible for every job it is applied to.
plan_content.title: Backward gate-walk diagnosis of the red CI - Affected run, then structural removal of dead Redis/NATS service coupling from gate jobs that never use them
plan_content.validation_plan: Canonical suite as declared: npx nx affected --target=test, npx nx affected --target=lint, node tools/quality/quality.mjs format check-changed, all expected exit 0. Because the changed path is workflow YAML, the observable proof is: (a) the suite exits 0 with a diff confined to services-block deletions; (b) YAML remains valid (the lint/format gates and GitHub's own workflow parser on the next run); (c) on the next docs-only change, the docs-check job log shows no redis/nats service containers being started while the job still runs markdownlint-changed.mjs to completion; (d) the run-level aggregates (merge-gate, build-status) are green when their asserted lanes are green or skipped, with docs-check no longer able to redden the run for container-registry reasons.

risks.recommendation: The primary's next revision must state architectural_tier (1-4) and justify it; if it adopts the challenger's structural services-removal fix, tier 1 is the honest claim, matching the challenger's justification.

plan_content.architectural_approach: Tier 3 (detectable). The wrong state — a filtered-lane ceiling that exceeds the SSOT bound, or one starved below the measured worst case — is caught at test time by an existing, already-wired owner: tests/invariants/ci-timeout-budget-ssot.spec.ts enforces the filtered ≤ unfiltered relation and runs under `npx nx affected --target=test`. The change re-baselines the constant inside that enforced relation rather than adding a parallel mechanism (a lane-side assertion step duplicating the spec would add maintenance surface with no new detection — the spec is the reuse target, per existing-owner discipline). Tier 1 is unavailable: no type system or compiler constrains a YAML integer. Tier 2 is unavailable at this scope: deriving the ceiling automatically at workflow-parse time would require a shared config or composite action outside the single allowed file.
plan_content.context: Think of this workflow as a chain of reporters ending in one originator. The red you see on a failed 'CI - Affected' run is emitted by the aggregation jobs: merge-gate's 'Assert required PR checks' loop and build-status's 'Assert affected validation status' step (line 2046) — but these loops only restate upstream job results (success/skipped checks, with install/lint/type-check/test/build required strictly success when has_changes=true). Repairing a reporter never fixes a run; you must walk backward to the job whose result they are restating. I traversed in that direction — assertion jobs first (2022/2046, then 1348/1363), gated jobs next (docs-check at 1655/1694), the changed job last (test at 368). Among the asserted jobs, only the test job shows an in-file defect signal: its timeout-minutes: 45 is a hand-calibrated constant whose own comment cites measurements taken before the suite grew, and the repository's own history (commit b5be2c1fdfa8, INFRA-MEDIUM-205) records that the suite outgrew that calibration badly enough to force a re-derivation of CI-Full's budgets. Why the filtered lane hits a full-suite-scale ceiling: on push-to-main, detect-changes resolves the affected range from the deployed/development tag, so a push landing after several undeployed merges sees an affected set close to the whole workspace. When that set's tests run past minute 45, the runner kills the job; merge-gate and build-status then correctly report test result=failure and the run is red. If this is skipped, every broad PR and main push keeps dying at minute 45 — merges blocked not because code is broken but because the ceiling is stale. The downstream surfaces affected are the required PR checks, the merge queue (merge-gate), build-status, and — on push runs with deploy changes — the development delivery chain asserted at 1348/1363. The proof that the fix is correct is machine-checkable: tests/invariants/ci-timeout-budget-ssot.spec.ts runs inside `npx nx affected --target=test` and fails the suite if the filtered lane's budget exceeds the unfiltered lane's, so a wrong constant cannot land green.

plan_content.recursive_impact: The edited constant is consumed only by the GitHub Actions runner scheduling the test job. No nx project imports or depends on the workflow file, no event contract, GraphQL surface, DB entity, or migration is coupled to it, and the coverage closure over .github/workflows/ci-affected.yml yields no project, event-consumer, or migration nodes (hence the empty waiver list). The jobs whose behavior changes are the downstream aggregators — merge-gate, build-status, and on push runs development-delivery-status — and they change only in that `test` stops being killed mid-suite; their assertion logic is untouched. Per-step timeouts inside the test job (including the 20-minute integration/Testcontainers bound) are deliberately left as-is so hang detection strength is unchanged.
